item.title: Fuel hike hits commuters, freight before new fares take effect
item.description:
The government’s latest fuel price hike has begun feeding through the economy within days, with bus passengers paying up to Tk100 more and freight operators charging thousands of taka extra even before revised transport fares have been officially finalized.
The September 20 increase of Tk20 per litre across four petroleum products pushed diesel, the lifeblood of road transport, irrigation and much of the country’s goods movement, from Tk115 to Tk135 per litre.
Petrol rose to Tk160, octane to Tk165 and kerosene to Tk155.
But the first shock is already visible beyond filling stations.
Higher charges have appeared at bus terminals and wholesale markets, while calculations by transport operators show the additional diesel bill for a long-distance bus can run into thousands of taka per round trip.
Economists and businesses warn the impact could spread further through food prices, agricultural production and industrial costs at a time when inflation remains above 8%.
At Gabtoli Bus Terminal on Monday, long-distance passengers were being charged Tk50-Tk100 more depending on their destinations, with both air-conditioned and non-AC operators seeking higher fares.
Md Ramzan, a passenger travelling from Kushtia, said he had paid Tk500 to travel to Dhaka the previous day but was charged Tk100 more for the same journey following the fuel price increase.
Bangladesh Bus-Truck Owners Association Chairman GR Shahid said operators would face losses if fares remained unchanged after the diesel price hike, adding that a revised fare chart would be announced soon.
The Bangladesh Road Transport Authority’s committee has proposed increasing long-distance bus fares by 20 poisha per kilometre and city bus fares by 18 poisha per kilometre.
A final decision is expected from the Road Transport and Bridges Ministry.
The arithmetic explains why operators are pressing for higher fares.
Transport operators estimate that a typical 45-seat long-distance bus travels around 3.5 kilometres on a litre of diesel.
At the previous Tk115 price, its fuel cost was around Tk32.86 per kilometre.
At Tk135, that rises to Tk38.57, an additional Tk5.71 for every kilometre travelled.
That translates into roughly Tk571 in additional fuel expenditure for every 100 kilometres.
The burden grows sharply on longer routes.
The Gabtoli-Panchagarh distance, for example, is around 438 kilometres, according to Roads and Highways Department data.
A round trip can consume more than 250 litres of diesel.
Even using 250 litres as the benchmark, the Tk20 increase adds around Tk5,000 to the fuel bill for a single round trip.
For a bus carrying about 50 passengers, that alone is equivalent to an additional Tk100 per passenger.
If the bus operates 25 such round trips a month, its additional diesel bill could reach around Tk125,000.
Bus owner Md Kamrul Islam Babul said operators had little room to absorb the increase without adjusting fares.
Bangladesh Road Transport Owners Association Secretary General Md Saiful Alam said transport businesses were already struggling with rising operating costs and called for a mechanism to automatically adjust fares in line with fuel prices.
The repercussions are potentially more significant in goods transport, where higher freight costs can eventually be passed on to consumers.
At Chittagong’s Khatunganj wholesale market, the cost of transporting a truckload of goods from Kushtia has increased from Tk32,000 to Tk40,000, according to warehouse manager Nurul Islam.
Freight charges on different routes have increased by between Tk2,000 and Tk8,000.
Transporting 265 sacks of rice from Kushtia to Dhaka now costs around Tk22,000, up from Tk20,000.
A covered van carrying 10.5 tons of garments from Benapole to Kanchpur is charging around Tk22,000, compared with Tk18,000-Tk19,000 previously.
Truck driver Mohammad Nazmus Zaman said a Satkhira-Chattogram round trip consumes about 230 litres of diesel.
The new price therefore adds approximately Tk4,600 to his fuel bill for each round trip.
Businesses say they cannot absorb such increases indefinitely, raising the prospect that additional freight costs will eventually be incorporated into wholesale and retail prices.
The impact does not end with buses and trucks.
Bangladesh has an estimated 1.3-1.5 million diesel-powered irrigation machines, while agriculture and irrigation account for around 15% of diesel demand, according to government figures cited in the report.
The higher price will therefore raise irrigation costs for diesel-dependent farmers, while factories and businesses relying on diesel generators and machinery will also face higher operating expenses.
Dhaka University Economics Professor Selim Raihan warned that the increase comes after several years of elevated inflation, leaving households with limited capacity to absorb another round of higher costs.
He identified low-income urban households, informal-sector workers and farmers dependent on diesel-powered irrigation as particularly vulnerable.
Raihan said that while higher fuel prices could ease some of the government’s financial burden, the broader effects could include higher inflation, declining purchasing power and greater inequality.
State Minister for Power, Energy and Mineral Resources Anindya Islam Amit has said the government had little alternative to adjusting domestic prices because international fuel costs had risen amid the Middle East crisis.
According to the Energy Division, importing a litre of diesel currently costs around Tk205. At the new retail price of Tk135, the government says it is still absorbing a loss of about Tk70 per litre.
International oil prices, however, fell on Monday, with November futures dropping 2.11% to around $98 a barrel, compared with $109 on September 15.
The price increase has also revived questions over taxes on fuel and inefficiencies in the distribution system.
The National Board of Revenue collects taxes and duties equivalent to 25% on refined petroleum and 27.5% on crude oil. Government revenue from imported diesel amounts to around Tk38 per litre in duties and taxes.
FBCCI Administrator Md Fazlul Hoque said increasing retail prices should not automatically be considered the only solution, arguing that the government should also look at reducing waste and system losses in fuel supply and distribution.
Bangladesh has seen the inflationary consequences of major fuel adjustments before. In August 2022, diesel prices were increased by 42.5%, or Tk34 per litre, followed by increases in transport and production costs.
Inflation subsequently rose from 7.5% to 9.5%, according to the figures cited in the report.
This time, the first round of higher costs has arrived almost immediately.
With inflation already above 8%, the bigger concern is what follows as the Tk20-a-litre increase works its way from diesel pumps into buses, trucks, irrigation fields, factories and, eventually, household bills.

item.title: President stresses job-oriented education to boost employment
item.description:
President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir on Tuesday stressed the need for greater emphasis on technology, engineering and technical education aimed at creating employment opportunities both at home and abroad.
“We have to gradually move away from an education system that creates unemployment and does not equip students for employment,” he said.
The president made the remarks when a delegation led by Pabna University of Science and Technology Vice-Chancellor Prof Dr Abul Hasnat Mohammad Shamim paid a courtesy call on him at Bangabhaban.
During the meeting, the VC briefed the president on the overall academic activities of the university.
The president said the quality of education must be improved in line with the rapidly changing world so that students of the country can move forward.
The vice-chancellor formally invited the president, who is also the Chancellor of the university, to attend its upcoming convocation.
The president accepted the invitation and assured that he would attend the convocation.
The president’s military secretary, secretary and press secretary, as well as the university’s Pro-Vice-Chancellor and Treasurer, were present.

item.title: Govt steps up efforts to modernize shipping sector
item.description:
Bangladesh is pursuing a broad modernization of its shipping sector, combining new deep-sea and container terminals with dredging, expanded port capacity, digitalisation and improved inland waterways to strengthen the country’s trade infrastructure.
According to the FY2026-27 budget document, the government has adopted a series of initiatives to increase cargo and container-handling capacity, improve vessel-handling efficiency, expand dredging activities and increase port-yard capacity.
The broader plan also covers development of sea and land ports, modernisation of river ports and launch terminals, maintenance of inland waterways and strengthening of safety and institutional capacity.
Around 95% of Bangladesh’s total import and export activities are conducted through Chittagong and Mongla ports, making their capacity and efficiency particularly important for the country’s trade and economy.
Chittagong faces growing pressure
Chittagong Port, the country’s principal maritime gateway, has already experienced a sharp increase in cargo and container handling over the years.
According to figures presented by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman in Parliament in July, the port handled 138.152 million tons of cargo and 3.409 million TEUs of containers in 2025, compared with 45.396 million tons and 1.343 million TEUs respectively in 2010.
Container handling increased 4.07%, cargo handling 11.43% and ship handling 10.5% in 2025 compared with the previous year, he said.
The port operates 24 hours a day, seven days a week, and the government is taking a number of measures to increase its capacity and efficiency.
These include the operation of the Patenga Container Terminal, development of the Laldia Container Terminal, regular capital and maintenance dredging, procurement of new cargo and container-handling equipment and digitalisation of port services, according to the prime minister’s statement in Parliament.
The government is also taking measures to ease container congestion by improving yard management and speeding up cargo clearance.
Shipping Minister Shaikh Rabiul Alam told Parliament in July that around 80% of container unloading and delivery operations at Chittagong Port had already been digitalised, with work underway to cover the remaining 20%.
The government is encouraging delivery of import containers through private inland container depots and off-docks, while more than 10,000 TEUs of long-staying containers inside the port are planned to be auctioned through customs to free up yard space.
The planned Chittagong Bay Terminal is expected to become one of the most important components of the country’s maritime expansion.
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman said the terminal would allow large mother vessels to berth directly at Chittagong Port, reducing transshipment costs and accelerating import and export activities.
At present, many large vessels cannot enter Chittagong because of navigational limitations.
Once completed, the two facilities are expected to receive vessels with drafts of 12 to 14 metres and reduce vessel waiting time through direct berthing, the minister said.
The Laldia Container Terminal is another major component of the planned expansion of Chittagong Port.
Construction of the terminal, one of Bangladesh’s largest public-private partnership investments involving more than $550 million, formally began in August.
The terminal is being developed with Danish cooperation and is expected to introduce modern equipment and technology into port operations.
Under the concession agreement, the project covers three years of construction and 30 years of operation, with a provision for a further 15-year extension, Shipping Minister Shaikh Rabiul Alam said in Parliament.
The government sees the terminal as part of its effort to increase capacity and bring international expertise and modern operational practices into the country’s port sector.
The Matarbari Deep Seaport in Cox’s Bazar represents another major shift in Bangladesh’s maritime infrastructure.
The under-construction port is expected to begin operations by 2029, according to the shipping minister.
It will have a navigational channel about 16 metres deep and will be capable of accommodating container vessels carrying around 8,200 TEUs or cargo ships of up to 100,000 deadweight tons. Such vessels are nearly four times larger than those currently handled at Chittagong Port, according to the minister.
The facility is expected to reduce Bangladesh’s dependence on foreign transshipment hubs such as Colombo, Singapore and Port Klang by allowing large mother vessels to call directly at a Bangladeshi port.
The government expects this to reduce shipping time and transshipment-related logistics costs while improving the country’s competitiveness in international trade.
Matarbari could also provide opportunities for regional transit and trade, potentially strengthening Bangladesh’s position as a maritime hub in South Asia.
Mongla Port is also undergoing major expansion to increase its role in Bangladesh’s maritime trade.
The projects are expected to increase the port’s capacity substantially, with plans targeting annual handling of up to 800,000 TEUs of containers, 4 million metric tons of cargo and 30,000 vehicles.
Two of the six additional jetties were under construction, with the work expected to further increase the port’s container-handling capacity.
The Mongla Port Upgradation Project has also targeted annual handling capacity of 1.5 million tons of cargo and 400,000 TEUs of containers.
Payra Port is another key part of the government’s maritime development strategy.
The government plans maintenance dredging of the Rabnabad Channel and procurement of two trailing suction hopper dredgers to ensure uninterrupted navigability and strengthen the port’s operational capacity, Shipping Minister Shaikh Rabiul Alam told Parliament in June.
The Payra Port Authority is implementing a number of projects aimed at establishing a fully fledged seaport.
The planned dredging is particularly important because maintaining the required channel depth is a continuing challenge for a port located in a heavily silted riverine environment.
Dredging is emerging as one of the most important elements of the government’s water transport strategy.
Apart from port channels, the government has undertaken a broader programme of river and canal excavation and re-excavation.
The Water Resources Ministry has set a target of excavating and re-excavating 20,000 kilometres of canals across the country over five years, according to an announcement made in Parliament.
Digitalization is another major pillar of the modernisation programme.
At Chittagong Port, online Port Community System, e-delivery orders, e-payment services, e-gate passes, CPA SKY and the Port Single Window are being introduced as part of efforts to establish a paperless port, according to the Prime Minister’s statement in Parliament.
The government has also initiated steps to automate overall port operations and procure additional cargo and container-handling equipment.
The modernization plan also places emphasis on institutional capacity.
The government plans to modernise vessel registration systems, expand digital services, develop skills and generate employment opportunities for seafarers.
Safety on inland waterways is another priority, with plans to modernise river ports and launch terminals and strengthen navigational aids.
The Bangladesh Inland Water Transport Authority has also been instructed to take coordinated measures with relevant agencies to ensure the safety of vessels operating on waterways.

item.title: Titumir: LDC graduation must strengthen, not constrain development
item.description:
Prime Minister's Finance and Planning Adviser Dr Rashed Al Mahmud Titumir has stressed that graduation and sustainable graduation are different, saying that LDC graduation should strengthen, rather than constrain, a country’s development trajectory.
He made the comments at the LDC-GIF Mechanism Introduction & High-Level Dialogue at the United Nations Headquarters in New York on Monday.
Dr Titumir said graduating countries continue to face structural impediments and limited productive capacity, compounded by geopolitical conflicts, supply-chain disruptions, trade uncertainty, inflation and domestic shocks.
He emphasized that graduation must therefore be supported by adequate measures to ensure a smooth, sustainable and irreversible transition through industrialization, integrated approaches, energy transition and job creation.
The adviser also called for stronger financial, technological and capacity-building support for LDCs, noting that actual technology transfer remains modest compared with their needs.
He expressed hope that the LDC Green Industrialisation Facilitation (LDC-GIF) mechanism would accelerate technology transfer, deployment and industrial application, while supporting productive capacity, structural transformation and sustainable graduation.

item.title: Man found dead in Dhanmondi Lake
item.description:
Police on Tuesday morning recovered a man’s body from Dhanmondi Lake in Dhaka.
The deceased has been identified as Javed, a resident of Pallabi in Mirpur.
The body was recovered from the lake at around 6:30am, said Dhanmondi police station Sub-Inspector SM Abdul Gafur.
He said police received a report through the national emergency hotline 999 at around 6:30am and found the body floating in the lake under a bridge near Road 10.
“With the help of local residents, we brought the body to the lakeside stairs,” he said.
Police found an identity card and a mobile phone number in Javed’s pocket and contacted his family. His wife later arrived at the scene and identified the body.
The body was sent to the Dhaka Medical College Hospital morgue for an autopsy, along with the necessary documents.
The exact cause of death will be known after the autopsy, the police official said.

item.title: Dhaka ranks 18th in global pollution list
item.description:
Dhaka ranked 18th among the world's most polluted cities on Tuesday morning, recording an Air Quality Index (AQI) score of 86 at 11:30am.
The air quality was classified as "Moderate", indicating that the air quality is generally acceptable, although unusually sensitive people may experience some health effects, according to the AQI scale.
Pakistan's Lahore topped the list with an AQI score of 181.
India’s Delhi and Hanoi of the Vietnam ranked second and third, respectively, with AQI scores of 181 and 177.
According to AQI standards, a reading between 101 and 150 is considered 'unhealthy for sensitive groups', while 151 to 200 is classified as 'unhealthy'. A reading between 201 and 300 is considered 'very unhealthy', while levels above 301 are deemed 'hazardous', posing serious health risks.
The AQI provides daily updates on air quality, indicating how clean or polluted the air is and highlighting potential health impacts.
In Bangladesh, the AQI is calculated based on five major pollutants: particulate matter (PM10 and PM2.5), nitrogen dioxide (NO2), carbon monoxide (CO), sulfur dioxide (SO2) and ozone.
Dhaka has long struggled with air pollution, with air quality typically deteriorating during winter and improving during the monsoon season.
The World Health Organization estimates that air pollution causes around seven million deaths globally each year, mainly from stroke, heart disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, lung cancer and acute respiratory infections.

item.title: Over 8,000 patients, no measles testing facilities in Chittagong hospitals
item.description:
The number of patients admitted to hospitals in Chittagong with measles symptoms is rising daily, but neither public nor private hospitals in the city have facilities to test for and confirm the disease.
As a result, samples from suspected cases must be sent to the National Polio and Measles-Rubella Laboratory (NPML) in Dhaka, delaying diagnosis and complicating treatment management.
The Bangladesh Institute of Tropical and Infectious Diseases (BITID) in Sitakunda, Chittagong, has a laboratory capable of detecting measles. However, testing is not currently being conducted there, leaving the Chittagong health department dependent on Dhaka.
According to the District Civil Surgeon’s Office, another 70 patients with measles symptoms were admitted to hospitals in Chittagong in the past 24 hours, bringing the total number of patients admitted with such symptoms to 7,941.
Eighteen people have died in the region. Of them, 15 died while undergoing treatment after showing measles symptoms, while three had tested positive for the disease.
So far, samples from 1,960 people—1,645 from the city and 315 from the district—have been sent to the NPML in Dhaka. Most of the test reports have already been received.
Chittagong Divisional Health Officer Dr Sekh Fazle Rabbi told Bangla Tribune that laboratory testing is not currently being conducted for measles in Chittagong.
“Measles is not currently being diagnosed through laboratory testing in Chittagong. Testing is not necessary in every case, as doctors can identify the disease based on symptoms. However, in accordance with government policy, patients seeking treatment with these symptoms are being treated for measles,” he said.
He added: “For patients who wish to undergo testing, samples are collected and sent to the National Polio and Measles-Rubella Laboratory (NPML) in Dhaka. Reports are received within two to three days.”
Saifuddin, a resident of Raozan Upazila, said he had his three-month-old daughter tested at a private laboratory late last month after she developed measles symptoms on a doctor’s advice.
“The sample was sent to Dhaka. The test cost Tk4,500, and it took a week to receive the report,” he said.
He added: “Although my daughter had symptoms, the doctor could not definitively confirm measles, which is why the test was ordered. Measles testing is expensive. Since the test is not available in Chittagong, there is a delay in getting results, which can cause a patient’s condition to deteriorate.”
Jamal Uddin, a resident of Jamal Khan under Kotwali police station, said: “Despite Chittagong being the country’s second-most populous city, measles testing facilities have not been established here. Yet 50 to 70 people are admitted to hospitals every day with measles symptoms. Beyond those hospitalized, many more are receiving treatment at home.”
The Bangladesh Institute of Tropical and Infectious Diseases (BITID), established in 2013 at Faujdarhat in Chittagong, is equipped to treat various infectious diseases, including measles and rubella.
The institute has real-time PCR and ELISA machines, as well as Rudolf Merieux laboratory facilities, including GeneXpert for tuberculosis detection and automated blood analyzers.
Professor Dr Mamunur Rashid of BITID told Bangla Tribune that doctors can diagnose measles based on its characteristic symptoms.
“The three primary symptoms are high fever, coughing and a rash. Typically, the rash begins around the face and ears before spreading to other parts of the body. The presence of these symptoms generally indicates a measles infection,” he said.
He added: “BITID’s laboratory is capable of conducting measles tests, but we currently do not have the necessary kits for measles-rubella testing. A request for the kits has been sent to Dhaka. Testing can begin once the kits and necessary approvals are received.”

item.title: Trump to tout deals, defend Iran war in UN speech
item.description:
US President Donald Trump is expected to claim he is winning both on the battlefield and as a peacemaker Tuesday in a speech to the United Nations overshadowed by growing spillover from his stalled war against Iran.
Trump will likely not hold back in renewing his frequent boasts that under him the United States is "the hottest country" in the world.
He is also expected to seek to justify the Iran war, which has so far failed to fulfil White House objectives and provoked widespread economic damage over the Strait of Hormuz's closure.
But the self-styled peacemaker could equally use the UN stage to tout his controversial efforts to end the Gaza conflict and his ongoing effort to bring more Arab countries into the Abraham Accords with Israel.
"No one knows what Trump is going to say, not even Trump's speechwriters," International Crisis Group's Daniel Forti said.
"This year, we expect more of a contrast between Trump, sort of both announcing and celebrating his record as a peacemaker versus defending his ongoing military operations around the world," said Forti.
"It's not entirely clear what reaction Trump's going to get from world leaders."
The keynote speech at the start of the UN General Assembly High-level week will provide Trump with a big platform to renew his frequent assaults on the global body.
Last year's speech was characterized by Trump's extraordinary accusations of UN sabotage when an escalator in the New York headquarters briefly stopped working and the teleprompter glitched.
Trump has regularly attacked the UN and its leader Antonio Guterres since returning to office, although Washington last week reportedly paid $725 million into its budget, avoiding the embarrassment of losing some of its voting rights.
He is also likely to meet skepticism over his claims of a historic win for the United States when a security deal is signed Tuesday for a US presence in Greenland -- a territory of Denmark that Trump repeatedly threatened, driving bitter divisions through longtime US-led alliances.
As well as his closely watched speech to the General Assembly, Trump will hold side meetings with Britain's new prime minister, Andy Burnham, as well as Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, Japanese premier Sanae Takaichi and Venezuela's interim leader Delcy Rodriguez.
Rodriguez has governed under intense American pressure since her predecessor Nicolas Maduro was captured by US forces in January.
Last year, Trump's speech to the gathering of world leaders veered into a rant about an escalator that stalled as he was using it, suggesting it was done deliberately.
He also railed against a defective teleprompter, falsely accused London's mayor of imposing Islamic law and said Europe was in "serious trouble" over migration.
Trump clearly has not gotten over the incidents.
"They turned off the escalator," Trump said last week in the Oval Office.
"Fortunately, my first lady was very strong and I was able to grab her back or another part of her body. It was actually a little bit lower than the back," he said.
The offending escalator "has been checked and rechecked," Guterres's spokesman Stephane Dujarric said Monday.
"New arrangements were made to facilitate the US delegation's use of a teleprompter, they now have a separate booth, so we hope that will work without a hitch," he added.
Guterres, who kicks off the week of speeches, is expected to touch on the explosion of artificial intelligence and the multiple wars raging globally.
Next up -- just before Trump -- will be Brazilian President Lula Inacio Lula da Silva, whose country by tradition is always first to speak at the annual gathering of leaders.
Trump, who has supported Lula's opponents and other right-wing candidates across Latin America, may not like what he hears.
Leftist Lula, running for reelection, said last week that he would tell Trump to not "meddle" in Brazil's upcoming vote.

item.title: Gazi Nazrul’s wife Mariam laid to rest in family graveyard
item.description:
Embattled MP and suspended Jamaat leader Gazi Nazrul Islam’s second wife, Mariam, was buried beside her grandparents at their family graveyard in Gabura of Shyamnagar upazila early Tuesday.
An ambulance carrying her body left Dhaka on Monday afternoon and reached Kashirhatkhola in Koyra, Khulna.
The body was then taken by a trawler along the river route to her family home in Gabura around 11:30pm.
With police security and assistance from local residents, family members completed the bathing and funeral prayers for Mariam shortly after the body arrived.
She was then buried beside her grandparents at the family graveyard.
Former village police member Golam Rahman said Mariam had lived in Dhaka since childhood.
“She used to study in Dhaka and had also appeared in the SSC examination. I cannot accept that such a tragedy happened to her at such a young age,” he said.
Her body was recovered from the MP’s flat at the NAM Bhaban in Sher-e-Bangla Nagar in the capital on Sunday evening.
Following the incident, her father Masum Billah filed a case with Sher-e-Bangla Nagar Police Station accusing three people of abetting her suicide.
The accused are her husband MP Gazi Nazrul Islam; his first wife Maksuda Begum; and Mariam’s maternal uncle Obaidur Rahman.
Gazi Nazrul Islam was elected MP from the Satkhira-4 constituency in the 13th parliamentary election on a Jamaat-e-Islami nomination.
Police arrested Gazi Nazrul and Maksuda after the case was filed and produced them before a court.
The court subsequently granted four days’ remand for Gazi Nazrul and one day’s remand for Maksuda. Obaidur Rahman remains absconding.
In July, a video showing him in a private moment with a young woman circulated on social media. He later identified the woman as his second wife Mariam Khatun.
Jamaat-e-Islami subsequently expelled Gazi Nazrul Islam from the party.

item.title: MP Nazrul, first wife accused of torturing second wife, abetting suicide
item.description:
The father of lawmaker Gazi Nazrul Islam’s second wife, Mariam, has accused the MP, his first wife Maksuda Islam and matchmaker Obaidur Rahman of physically and mentally torturing his daughter and abetting her suicide.
Mariam’s father Masum Billah filed the case with Sher-e-Bangla Nagar police naming Nazrul Islam, 75, as the prime accused, Maksuda Islam, 65, as the second accused and Obaidur Rahman, 38, as the third accused.
In the first information report (FIR), Masum said he is a grocery shop owner and has three daughters. Mariam, 19, was his eldest daughter.
He identified Nazrul as Mariam’s husband and Maksuda as his first wife, while describing Obaidur as his brother-in-law.
According to the FIR, Mariam married Nazrul in June under Islamic Shariah. Nazrul, who is a lawmaker, lived with Mariam and his first wife at Flat 203 on the third floor of Building 5 of NAM Bhaban, opposite the National Parliament complex on Manik Mia Avenue under Sher-e-Bangla Nagar police station.
Masum alleged that Obaidur directly instigated the marriage. He said Mariam had repeatedly told her family over the phone that Nazrul and Maksuda subjected her to physical and mental torture after the marriage.
The FIR said Nazrul called Masum at around 5:30pm on Sunday and asked him to come to the residence immediately. Masum then went there by CNG-run auto-rickshaw with his sister-in-law Sufia.
Upon reaching the residence, Masum saw a large number of people and learned that Mariam was hanging from a ceiling fan by a scraf inside a room. He said she was shown through a window and that the room was locked from inside.
In Masum’s presence, witness Md Saidul Islam, 36, broke open the door with the help of Sher-e-Bangla Nagar police, the FIR said. Saidul is a temporary plumber employed by the Public Works Department (PWD), according to the complaint.
Masum said they found Mariam hanging from the ceiling fan with a scarf around her neck. A handwritten suicide note was also found on her bed.
The note reportedly accused someone of betraying Mariam’s trust and referred to a “battle” she had entered believing she would win. “I kept bowing to you again and again because I fell for you. Otherwise, I am not as cheap as you think,” the note reportedly said. It further said: “I entered the battle with him, trusting him completely, but I could not win.”
The note contained further writings, the FIR said.
Masum alleged that after questioning people at the scene, he learned that Mariam might have died by suicide sometime between 3:00pm and 5:30pm.
Later, Sher-e-Bangla Nagar police visited the scene, prepared an inquest report and sent Mariam’s body to the morgue, according to the FIR.

item.title: 17th International Inter-University Short Film Festival begins
item.description:
The 17th International Inter-University Short Film Festival (IIUSFF) began at the TSC premises of Dhaka University on Monday evening, with speakers discussing the festival’s journey and the role of cinema in truth-telling and preserving cultural memory.
Organized by the Dhaka University Film Society (DUFS), the festival began in 2007 in a small room on the 2nd floor of TSC with the slogan “Take Your Camera, Frame Your Dream.”
DUFS President Rehnuma Shahreen said 1,269 films from 92 countries, including Bangladesh, Iran, the United States and Poland, were submitted to this year’s festival.
She said the scale of the festival would have been unimaginable in 2007, when opportunities for communication and networking were limited.
The 3-day main event, running from September 21 to 23, features open screenings of 200 selected short films, discussions with student filmmakers and a live art camp.
The festival is being held with support from UNDP Bangladesh, the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR) and the Royal Norwegian Embassy in Dhaka.
Speaking as a guest, film critic and teacher Bidhan Rebeiro referred to the recently released documentary “Naza.”
He said the documentary has sparked debate worldwide by featuring testimonies from former Israeli intelligence officials about the use of artificial intelligence in attacks on Gaza, while its filmmakers have faced threats.
According to Rebeiro, the term “Naza” is used in intelligence circles to describe civilian casualties in such attacks.
He said the Israeli government had threatened to revoke the filmmakers’ citizenship and completely ban the production after the documentary was screened at the Venice and Toronto film festivals.
Rebeiro described the documentary as a “poetry of resistance” and praised its restrained visual language for challenging the global system of aggression.
He also linked this year’s festival theme, “Baul,” to the word “batul,” meaning madness, and said it reflected the social attitudes faced by people in Bangladesh who are interested in studying or pursuing careers in film.
He said cinema should be recognized as a complete and independent discipline rather than merely a vocational subject.
Teacher and film society movement activist Moinuddin Khaled discussed the difference between documentaries and propaganda.
He expressed regret that, despite documentaries being at the roots of cinema, Bangladesh lacks strong documentary records of its folk life and riverine civilization, including group fishing, jute cultivation and boat races.
Referring to Baul music and Lalon songs, he said: “The day we lose Baul songs, we will lose our greatest means of self-expression.”
He described farmers and fishermen as the 2 main pillars sustaining the civilization of the nation.

Pubali Bank, BB sign agreements under two refinance schemes
item.description:
To expand financing for sustainable industrialization, environment-friendly production and the development of a technology-driven economy, Pubali Bank PLC. has joined Bangladesh Bank’s ‘Refinance Scheme for Green Factory Building and Green Industry Sector’ and ‘Refinance Scheme for Development of the Information and Communication Technology Sector’.
Each scheme has a fund size of Tk1,000 crore.
Pubali Bank has signed separate Participation Agreements with Bangladesh Bank for the two schemes administered by the Sustainable Finance Department of Bangladesh Bank.
At the agreement signing ceremony held at the Bangladesh Bank Head Office on the same day, Director of the Sustainable Finance Department of Bangladesh Bank AKM Nurunnabi and managing director of Pubali Bank PLC Mohammad Ali signed the agreements on behalf of their respective institutions.
Also present were deputy managing director of Pubali Bank PLC Mohammad Esha and general manager & head of RMG Division Md Nazrul Islam Sarker, along with other senior officials of Bangladesh Bank and Pubali Bank.
To support the implementation of various long-term plans announced by the Government of Bangladesh—including the Perspective Plan of Bangladesh, National Sustainable Development Strategy, Intended Nationally Determined Contributions (INDCs), Bangladesh Delta Plan 2100 and Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)—and to make the country’s financial sector more environment-friendly, Bangladesh Bank has established the Tk1,000 crore ‘Refinance Scheme for Green Factory Building and Green Industry Sector’ to encourage financing for green factory buildings and green industries.
The scheme will expand financing opportunities for the establishment of green factory buildings, green industries and other environmentally responsible industrial initiatives.
It is expected to promote green investment while further accelerating the adoption of sustainable production practices and responsible industrialization.
Meanwhile, under the ‘Refinance Scheme for Development of the Information and Communication Technology Sector’, Bangladesh Bank has established a Tk1,000 crore fund.
The scheme aims to enhance the efficiency and competitiveness of the ICT sector through the adoption of modern and sustainable technologies, develop human resources, expand technology-driven enterprises, and support the development of new technologies and services aligned with the Fourth Industrial Revolution.
The facility covers various technology-driven initiatives, including software development, artificial intelligence, cyber security, fintech, cloud computing, e-commerce, robotics and semiconductors.
Through participation in these two refinance schemes, Pubali Bank PLC. will further strengthen its role in expanding financing for environment-friendly industrial initiatives and the promising information and communication technology sector.
The initiatives are expected to widen access to financing for eligible entrepreneurs and institutions while contributing to sustainable industrialization, technological capacity building, innovation and employment generation in the country.

item.title: Ambassador: Brands like Walton should be promoted more in global market
item.description:
Bangladesh Ambassador to Nepal Md Shafiqur Rahman has called for concerted efforts to further strengthen the presence of Bangladeshi brands like Walton in the global market.
He said Walton has been doing remarkable work in Bangladesh’s hi-tech industry. By manufacturing international-standard technology products, the company reduced the country’s import dependency and saved a significant amount of foreign currency. At the same time, Walton is contributing to foreign currency earnings by exporting its products to different countries across the world.
The Ambassador made the remarks as the chief guest at a special program of Walton Plaza, Bangladesh’s leading sales and service provider of electronics and technology products, titled ‘Tushar Jatra’, held on Saturday (September 19) at The Soaltee in Kathmandu, Nepal.
Among others, SM Mahbubul Alam, managing director of Walton Hi-Tech Industries PLC and managing partner of Walton Plaza; Pranil Thapa, chairman of Nepal’s renowned Thapa Business Group; Pranimesh Thapa, director of Thapa Business Group; and senior officials of Walton attended the program.
Ambassador Md Shafiqur Rahman said: “Walton is doing remarkable work in Bangladesh’s hi-tech sector. The quality of Walton’s locally manufactured hi-tech products is top-notch. With these products, Walton is competing with other international brands in the global market and establishing a strong position. This is a matter of great pride for the people of Bangladesh.”
He further said that the local production of high-quality hi-tech products is reducing Bangladesh’s dependence on imports and saving a substantial amount of foreign currency. At the same time, Walton is earning foreign currency by exporting technology products to different countries around the world.
“Bangladeshi brands like Walton should be promoted more extensively in the international market. Bangladeshi ambassadors serving in different countries will also play a role in expanding the global market for local brands through economic diplomacy,” he added.
SM Mahbubul Alam, managing director of Walton Hi-Tech Industries PLC and managing partner of Walton Plaza, said Nepal is a highly important market for Walton. The company is working to make international-standard technology products available to Nepali consumers at affordable prices, just as it does in Bangladesh. Walton aims to further expand its operations in Nepal by building long-term relationships and mutual trust with local business partners.
Pranimesh Thapa, director of Thapa Business Group, said: “We are proud to have been part of Walton’s journey in Nepal for more than eight years. Thapa Business Group is committed to further expanding Walton’s presence across Nepal through innovative and quality products. We will continue working with our business partners to provide better services to customers and establish Walton as one of Nepal’s leading technology product brands.”
Md Rayhan, managing director of Walton Plaza, provided important guidelines to Walton Plaza officials, particularly on modern marketing and sales management.
Mofizur Rahman Jakir, deputy managing director of Walton Hi-Tech Industries PLC, and MM Nazmul Hasan, head of sales at Walton Plaza, also spoke at the program.
The event was conducted by Amin Khan, senior executive director of Walton Hi-Tech Industries PLC and noted film actor. It also featured a Nepal tour video presentation, raffle draw and cultural performances.

item.title: ONE Bank, BYD Bangladesh to facilitate new EV financing
item.description:
ONE Bank PLC has signed an MoU with BYD Bangladesh to facilitate convenient and attractive financing solutions for customers purchasing New Energy Vehicles (NEVs).
Under this collaboration, ONE Bank PLC will offer competitive interest rates and expedited loan processing facilities to customers purchasing BYD vehicles.
The initiative aims to make NEV financing more accessible and convenient for customers while supporting the adoption of environmentally friendly mobility solutions in Bangladesh.
On behalf of the two organizations, the MoU was signed by Amid Sakif Khan, managing director, BYD Bangladesh, and Mohammad Shahid Ul Haque, executive vice president & head of retail banking division of ONE Bank PLC.
The ceremony was also attended by Ferdowsur Rahman, chief financial officer; BYD Bangladesh; Methun Bhattacharjee, head of business development BYD Bangladesh; Kazi Ziaul Islam, deputy managing director and head of financial services and public sector; ONE Bank PLC; Iftekhar Ahmed Zafar, deputy managing director and head of transaction and investment banking, ONE Bank PLC, and senior officials from both the organizations.
BYD, a global leader in New Energy Vehicles (NEVs), entered the Bangladesh automobile market in 2024 through its official distributor.
The brand offers a growing range of advanced electric and plug-in hybrid vehicles, supported by modern showrooms and comprehensive after-sales service facilities.
With a strong focus on innovative technology, sustainable mobility, and energy-efficient transportation, BYD is contributing to the development of Bangladesh’s emerging electric vehicle market.
The collaboration between ONE Bank PLC and BYD Bangladesh reflects a shared commitment to promoting sustainable transportation and providing customers with accessible financing solutions for next-generation vehicles.

item.title: Nagad, IFIC Bank to introduce interoperable cardless cash withdrawal facility
item.description:
Nagad, one of Bangladesh’s leading mobile financial services (MFS) providers, has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with IFIC Bank PLC to launch an interoperable cardless cash withdrawal facility.
Under this agreement, Nagad customers will be able to withdraw cash from all IFIC Bank Automated Teller Machines (ATMs) across the country without using a physical card.
The agreement was signed at IFIC Bank’s head office in Dhaka.
High-ranking officials from both organizations were present at the signing ceremony, highlighting the strategic importance of this collaboration in enhancing financial inclusion and expanding digital banking services in Bangladesh.
Through this partnership, Nagad users can generate a secure, temporary transaction code or QR-based request via the Nagad mobile app to withdraw cash directly from IFIC Bank ATMs nationwide.
This initiative aims to provide customers with greater convenience, seamless interoperability between bank channels and mobile wallets, and enhanced security for cash transactions.
Speaking at the event, representatives from both Nagad and IFIC Bank emphasized their shared commitment to driving digital innovation, reducing dependence on physical cards, and building a more robust cashless ecosystem across the country.

item.title: Nationwide digital dengue awareness campaign launched
item.description:
A three-month nationwide digital awareness campaign has been launched to combat dengue, with State Minister for Health Dr MA Muhit urging citizens, particularly young people and social media content creators, to participate actively.
In a statement issued Monday, Muhit said dengue cannot be fully controlled through administrative measures or insecticide spraying alone, stressing the importance of individual and collective awareness.
He said social media can play a significant role in spreading timely information and reducing dengue risks, urging content creators and influencers to produce and share awareness materials, including videos, reels, stories, infographics and posts.
“Content creators can effectively communicate important messages on dengue prevention, including eliminating stagnant water and seeking medical attention promptly after symptoms appear,” the state minister said.
Many content creators have already joined the campaign facilitated by the Ministry of Health.
Over the next three months, social media platforms will be used to disseminate information on destroying Aedes mosquito breeding sites, recognizing dengue symptoms and providing initial care.
The state minister urged people to keep their homes and workplaces clean and help spread dengue prevention messages online as part of the national campaign.

item.title: Ashulia factory fire: Death toll rises to 8
item.description:
The death toll from a fire at a readymade garment factory in Jamgara of Ashulia has risen to eight after another victim died of his injuries on Sunday night.
The victim, a vegetable vendor whose identity could not immediately be known, succumbed to his injuries while undergoing treatment at Dhaka Medical College and Hospital, said Shahabuddin, senior station officer of Zirabo Fire Service.
The fire broke out at the F&F factory of Preeti Group in the Jamgara Chowrasta area at around 6:45pm on Sunday.
According to the Fire Service, the fire was triggered when a gas cylinder exploded while being unloaded from a covered van.
Four firefighting units rushed to the scene and brought the blaze under control around 3:30am.
Shahabuddin said firefighters struggled to reach the factory because of severe traffic congestion and poor road conditions, where construction work for the Ashulia Elevated Expressway is underway.
Litton Mia, a line man at a nearby garment factory and a witness, said the fire spread through the factory following a loud explosion of a gas cylinder.
The authorities are investigating the circumstances surrounding the fire.

item.title: Man kills mother, sister-in-law, 8-month-old niece in Comilla
item.description:
A man has allegedly hacked his mother and sister-in-law to death and killed his eight-month-old niece by slamming her against the ground in Debidwar, Comilla.
The incident occurred around 8:30am on Monday, at the house of late Mostafa Master in the southern part of Barshalghar village in the upazila.
Following the incident, local residents caught the accused, Imon, 24, red-handed and locked him inside a room. He is the son of the late Farid Mia of the same house.
According to locals, Imon’s mother, Peyaara Begum, and his eight-month-old niece died at the scene. His sister-in-law, Rabeya Begum, who sustained critical injuries in the attack, died on the way to hospital.
Local sources said Imon suddenly became agitated around 8:30am and hacked his mother to death with a machete. He then slammed his eight-month-old niece against the ground, killing her. When Rabeya Begum came forward to stop him, he attacked her indiscriminately with the machete, leaving her critically injured.
Locals later rescued Rabeya and rushed her to hospital for treatment, while detaining Imon in a nearby room.
Debidwar police station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Md Moniruzzaman confirmed the incident, saying police were on their way to the scene after receiving the report.
“Preliminarily, we have learned that Imon had been ill for a long time. However, it is not yet clear what prompted the brutal killings. The matter will become clear after we reach the scene and conduct a detailed investigation,” he said.

item.title: Bus set ablaze while parked in Narayanganj
item.description:
A Nilachal Paribahan bus was set ablaze while parked by the roadside in Siddhirganj, Narayanganj, early Monday.
The incident occurred around 2am on a new road beside the SO Eidgah ground in Ward 6 of Narayanganj City Corporation. No casualties were reported.
According to locals, the bus, which operates on the Chittagong Road-Paturia route, was parked by the roadside when miscreants allegedly set it on fire between 1:35am and 2am.
Two units from Adamjee Fire Station responded to the incident and brought the blaze under control. The bus was severely damaged, with its seats and other parts gutted by the fire.
Abdullah Al Arefin, deputy director of Narayanganj Fire Service, said the bus was extensively damaged, but no one was injured.
The cause of the fire has not yet been determined.
Confirming the incident, Tarek Al Mehedi, additional superintendent of police (Crime) of Narayanganj district, said: “We are reviewing CCTV footage to identify those involved in the incident. Legal action regarding the matter is currently underway.”

item.title: Gazi Nazrul, first wife arrested over second wife’s death
item.description:
A case has been filed on charges of abetting suicide following the recovery of the hanging body of Mariyam Khatun, second wife of Satkhira-4 MP Gazi Nazrul Islam, from a flat at the NAM Bhaban in the capital.
Mariyam’s father, Masum Billah, filed the case at Sher-e-Bangla Nagar Police Station late Sunday night. Gazi Nazrul, his first wife Maksuda Begum and Mariam’s maternal uncle Obaidur Rahman have been named as the three accused.
Dhaka Metropolitan Police Tejgaon Division Deputy Commissioner Md Ibne Mizan told the media that Gazi Nazrul and his first wife have been shown arrested, but Obaidur Rahman remains at large.
The 19-year-old woman, whom Satkhira-4 MP Gazi Nazrul Islam identified as his second wife amid a sensational controversy two months ago, was found hanging at his NAM Bhaban flat in Dhaka on Sunday, prompting police to take the lawmaker and his first wife to the police station for questioning.
Mariyam Khatun’s death brings Nazrul and the disputed circumstances surrounding their marriage back under scrutiny barely two months after the controversy led to his expulsion from Jamaat-e-Islami.
The controversy erupted on July 20 when video clips showing Nazrul in an intimate setting with a young woman began circulating widely on social media.
Nazrul subsequently identified the woman as Mariyam and rejected allegations that he was involved in an extramarital relationship. He said she was his legally married second wife.
According to Nazrul, he had married Mariyam on June 17 at her father’s residence in Shyamnagar, Satkhira, with the consent of both families and his first wife, Maksuda Islam.
Nazrul said that on July 13 he went with both wives to an office belonging to Mariyam’s father, Md Masum Billah, in Moghbazar.
He alleged that while they were there, Mariyam’s maternal uncle Obaidullah and several others entered the room, held them hostage and extorted Tk1 lakh.
He further alleged that demands for additional money followed and that private footage was later circulated because of a family dispute.
Maksuda subsequently appeared in a video message confirming that Nazrul had married Mariyam and protesting what she described as slander surrounding their relationship.
Mariyam herself also appeared publicly, wearing a face mask, and identified Nazrul as her husband.
She said the marriage was neither secret nor illicit and maintained that it had taken place with the consent of both families.
But questions subsequently emerged over the chronology of the marriage.
A CV attributed to Mariyam circulated online bearing Nazrul’s signature and a recommendation dated June 22, five days after the date on which Nazrul said they had married.
The CV reportedly listed her marital status as “unmarried”.
Further questions arose over the marriage registration.
The marriage registrar whose name appeared on the certificate later said he had not been present at the purported wedding and did not know when or where the marriage had taken place.
Reporting at the time said Nazrul maintained that the marriage occurred on June 17.
The controversy intensified as multiple video clips circulated.
In one, Nazrul and Mariyam were confronted by several men in a room.
Nazrul’s subsequent account was that the incident involved extortion and that the intimate footage had been distributed without consent.
The controversy quickly became a political crisis for Jamaat.
After initially saying it would investigate the allegations, the party’s Central Executive Council met on July 22 and expelled Nazrul under Article 62 of its constitution, saying an organisational investigation had found evidence of “moral misconduct”.
Jamaat subsequently formally informed both the Speaker and the Election Commission of the decision.
Nazrul had been elected from Satkhira-4 on Jamaat’s scales symbol in the February election.
His expulsion was described at the time as the first instance of Jamaat expelling one of its sitting lawmakers.
Two months after that controversy, the young woman at its centre has now been found dead inside the MPs’ residential complex.
CID forensic investigators reached the scene on Sunday evening as police began examining the circumstances surrounding Mariyam’s death.
With police yet to determine whether she took her own life or was killed, the cause and circumstances of her death remain under investigation.

"We agreed to meet in New York, and this meeting could change a lot. There is diplomatic momentum," he said.

item.title: Chevron Bangladesh launches Community Tree Guardianship initiative
item.description:
Chevron Bangladesh has launched a community-based Tree Guardianship initiative in partnership with Green Savers which is designed to expand green cover and support families living near its operational areas in Habiganj and Moulavibazar.
As part of the initiative, each Tree Guardian household will receive ten fruit bearing tree saplings, following a crop calendar, that includes mango, black plum (jamun), jackfruit, lychee, guava, lemon, hog plum (amra), custard apple, Indian gooseberry (amla) and jujube (boroi).
In total, 3,190 fruit tree saplings will be distributed, helping expand green cover while creating long-term environmental and socioeconomic benefits for participating families.
The participating households were selected following a field assessment that considered available space and the potential for long-term care of the trees.
Each participating family will serve as a "Tree Guardian” taking responsibility for household-level planting, protection and maintenance of the saplings.
The recently held event was graced by Md Abul Kalam Azad, director, Department of Environment (DoE), Sylhet Divisional Office as chief guest; Kaelie Knight Holder, general manager operations, Chevron Bangladesh; Muhammad Imrul Kabir, director, corporate affairs, Chevron Bangladesh; AKM Arif Akter, head of community engagement & sustainability, Chevron Bangladesh; Ahsan Rony, CEO of Green Savers, including other representatives from Department of Environment, Sylhet Forest Division, Mirzapur Union Parishad and representatives from Green Savers; employees of Chevron Bangladesh; and the dedicated Tree Guardians, whose efforts continue to support the long-term sustainability of the plantation initiative.
“Initiatives like this play an important role in advancing environmental sustainability and supporting the government’s goal of planting 250 million trees within five years. Through collective action and long-term commitment, we can build a greener, cleaner, and more sustainable Bangladesh,” said Md Abul Kalam Azad, director, Department of Environment (DoE), Sylhet Divisional Office.
Muhammad Imrul Kabir, director corporate affairs, Chevron Bangladesh, said: “This initiative reflects our commitment to working with neighboring communities to promote environmental stewardship and create meaningful benefits for participating families. By placing local residents at the center of the program, we hope to encourage long-term care of the trees and strengthen shared responsibility for the surrounding environment.”
“At Chevron Bangladesh, we believe safe and reliable operations are built on strong partnerships with the communities where we operate. Through the Tree Guardianship Program, we are working together to promote environmental stewardship, strengthen community partnerships, and create lasting value for future generations,” said Kaelie Knight Holder, general manager operations, Chevron Bangladesh.
As part of the initiative, Tree Guardians will receive practical training on soil preparation, plantation techniques, tree care, and long-term maintenance.
The community stewardship approach is intended to support tree survival while contributing to food security, household nutrition and potential supplementary income opportunities for participating families.
The Tree Guardianship initiative is designed to encourage community participation in environmental conservation and establish a greener landscape around pipeline-adjacent communities.
It also aims to strengthen local awareness and a sense of shared responsibility toward the safety and security of nearby pipeline infrastructure.

item.title: Opratim’s mother’s iPhone recovered from Tuhin’s home
item.description:
Police have recovered the iPhone belonging to 13-year-old Ishiyat Shahriar Opratim’s mother from the home of Tuhin, who was detained in connection with the boy’s death in Comilla.
Mofiz Uddin Bhuiyan, in-charge of the Kotbari Police Outpost, confirmed the matter on Saturday night.
He said police recovered the iPhone during a raid at Tuhin’s house in the Sananda area of Lalmai Hill, near Comilla University.
Opratim, a seventh-grade student at Comilla Border Guard Public School, had been missing since Friday afternoon. His body was found in Sananda area around 1:00pm on Saturday.
His mother, Dr Nahida Begum, is an associate professor in the Department of Bangla at Comilla University. She lived in a rented house in the Kotbari-Gandhamati area.
Police have detained three people Tuhin, Anas and Fahim in connection with the death. All three are aged between 18 and 20.
Inspector Mofiz Uddin said the other two were detained in the evening based on information obtained from Tuhin during questioning. Tuhin was detained around 3:00pm on Saturday.

item.title: Man held while “trying to set fire to bus” in Dhaka’s Azimpur
item.description:
Police detained a man early Sunday while he was allegedly attempting to set fire to a bus parked under Metanir overbridge in the capital’s Azimpur area.
The detainee was identified as Aminul Islam Shawon.
Police said Shawon was attempting to set fire to the bus around 2:15am when bus staff and local people noticed the incident and rushed to the spot.
Patrol police also arrived at the scene and detained him.
An agitated crowd beat up Shawon during the detention, leaving him injured, said Niaz Mehedi, additional deputy commissioner (Media) of Dhaka Metropolitan Police on Sunday afternoon.
He was later taken to Dhaka Medical College Hospital for treatment.

item.title: Measles outbreak: Death toll reaches 1,057 as four die in 24 hours
item.description:
Four more children have died from measles-like symptoms in the 24 hours leading up to 8:00am on Sunday, raising the overall death toll from the ongoing outbreak to 1,057.
The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) has classified all four of the latest casualties as suspected.
With the latest figures, the total number of suspected measles deaths has reached 956, while the number of confirmed deaths remained unchanged at 101, as no new confirmed measles deaths were reported in the last 24 hours.
Among the four new suspected fatalities, the highest concentration was recorded in Dhaka, with two deaths reported in both the Dhaka division and Dhaka district.
A total of 1,148 suspected measles cases were recorded in the 24 hours till Sunday morning, taking the overall suspected case tally to 179,814.
During the same period, 88 new confirmed measles cases were reported, bringing the total number of confirmed infections to 20,562.
Since March 15, 2026, a total of 158,589 suspected measles patients have been hospitalized across the country, of whom 152,225 have recovered and been discharged from hospitals, according to the DGHS.

item.title: Jatrabari crude bomb blasts: Four sent to jail, remand hearing Tuesday
item.description:
Four people, including a leader of the banned Awami League, have been sent to jail in a case filed over multiple crude bomb explosions in front of Jatrabari Police Station in Dhaka. The court has scheduled a hearing for Tuesday on a five-day remand plea against them.
Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Md Monirul Islam passed the order on Sunday.
The accused are Md Rayhan Uddin, 35, office secretary of the Awami League’s Unit 6 under Ward 32 of Bangshal Police Station area of Dhaka South City, Russell Khan, 32, Ala Uddin, 28, and Abdullah Mashhur Ashrafi, 20.
DB police Inspector Mohammad Golam Mostofa, investigation officer of the Wari zone, sought five days’ remand for the accused.
SI Mohin Uddin of the prosecution department confirmed the matter, saying, “The investigation officer did not appear before the court. Therefore, the accused were sent to jail and the remand hearing was scheduled for Tuesday.”
Several crude bombs exploded in front of Jatrabari Police Station on the night of September 18.
After identifying a suspect from CCTV footage, police arrested Rayhan Uddin during a raid in the Bangshal area on Saturday.
Based on information provided by Rayhan, police later recovered four unexploded crude bombs wrapped in red cellophane tape and concealed in a sack of brick chips beside a pillar in the ground-floor parking area of a 10-storey building on Zain Saha Road in Lalbagh around 12:15am. The DMP bomb disposal unit later defused the devices.
Acting on information obtained during Rayhan’s interrogation, police conducted a raid in the Dogair area of Demra and arrested Russell, Ala Uddin and Abdullah.
Meanwhile, Jatrabari Police Station SI Jewel Rana filed a case under the Explosives Act on Saturday over the crude bomb explosions.

item.title: Stakeholders call for stronger media self-regulation, accountability
item.description:
Media stakeholders have called for stronger self-regulation mechanisms to strengthen public trust in the media by ensuring editorial independence and accountability of owners, protecting journalists’ safety, and upholding professional standards.
They also agreed that enforcing editorial policies, ensuring transparency and accountability in management, and providing accessible grievance mechanisms can strengthen accountability in the news media.
They said these measures would help restore public trust by upholding ethical standards while balancing editorial independence with accountability.
The observations came at a divisional consultation held in Khulna by the Media Resources Development Initiative (MRDI) to discuss improving journalism’s professional and ethical standards and developing an effective framework for media self-regulation in Bangladesh.
MRDI launched the consultation series with the Khulna session under the Canada Fund for Local Initiatives, funded by the Canadian High Commission in Bangladesh.
News media owners and publishers, editors, news managers and gatekeepers, leaders of journalist unions and associations, university teachers and civil society representatives took part in the discussion.
MRDI Executive Director Hasibur Rahman called for continued advocacy on media self-regulation under the organization’s 2025–2030 strategic action plan, saying effective self-regulation would limit external interference.
He said press freedom depends on public trust, urging news outlets to establish accountability mechanisms and develop separate codes of conduct for journalists, editors and owners.
Speaking at the event, former Media Reform Commission chief and The Daily Star consulting editor Kamal Ahmed urged the government to quickly outline its plan for an independent Media Commission, saying it should promote self-regulation and allow the media to correct its own mistakes.
He criticised plans to increase penalties under the Cyber Security Act without clearly defining offences, warning that tougher laws alone would not resolve the media’s current challenges and could encourage self-censorship instead of self-regulation.
Participants agreed that sustainable self-regulation requires strong and independent editorial policies capable of resisting pressure from the government, media owners, advertisers and political actors.
Shamima Sultana Shilu, executive director of Manob Seba O Samajik Unnayan Sangstha, said journalists must perform their duties in a way that leaves no room for external interference while abiding by the law.
She stressed the importance of proper training before entering the journalism profession, saying it is essential for maintaining professional and ethical standards in journalism and ensuring responsible reporting.
On journalists’ working conditions, participants agreed that ethical journalism cannot be separated from financial security. They called on media owners to ensure timely payment of salaries, formal appointment letters, lawful benefits and a safe working environment.
Hedait Hossain Molla, joint secretary general of the Bangladesh Federal Union of Journalists, said a lack of transparency and integrity in media outlets’ financial practices undermines professionals’ rights and accountability.
He called for clear policies to protect the rights of news media professionals, noting that there is no specific legal framework governing appointment letters and that media organizations follow varying practices. He urged the development of a universal, legally compliant framework for appointment letters.
Sara Monami Hossain, head of the Department of Mass Communication and Journalism at Khulna University, said mainstream media, particularly national news organisations, have systems for information verification and fact-checking.
She said reliable and relevant information is more important in journalism than the volume of information, adding that journalists must assess whether information or an event is genuinely newsworthy before publishing or reporting it.
