item.title: Saleh: Media freedom doesn't mean arbitrary conduct
item.description:
Prime Minister’s Press Secretary Abu Abdullah M Saleh said on Thursday that the government supports full media freedom, but such freedom does not mean “arbitrary conduct.”
He made the remarks at a “Meet the Press” program organized by the Dhaka Reporters Unity (DRU) in the capital.
He said: “The responsibility of determining how far media freedom will extend does not lie with the government or the people; only the courts have the authority to make the final decision on this matter.”
Calling for measures to prevent the spread of false information in the era of information technology, Saleh said: “Every media outlet must take its own initiative to introduce a systematic ‘fact-checking’ program or information verification system to prevent rumors, speculation and misinformation. There is no alternative to this to ensure responsible journalism.”
Speaking about Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s participation in the upcoming session of the United Nations General Assembly, Saleh said: “Maintaining the traditional continuity of slain President Ziaur Rahman and former prime minister Begum Khaleda Zia, Prime Minister Tarique Rahman is going to address world leaders at the United Nations General Assembly this time. The participation of Bangladesh’s prime minister on the world stage is a matter of great pride not only for the country but also in the international context.”
Referring to the country’s economic and administrative situation, the press secretary said the government is moving the country forward by dealing with the fragile administrative structure of previous years and the ongoing global war situation.
He said Bangladesh has now become a highly safe and stable state for foreign investment after overcoming all types of domestic and international risks.

item.title: Ducsu publishes one-year activity and ‘accountability report’
item.description:
Dhaka University Central Students’ Union (Ducsu) has published a report outlining its activities and accountability over the past year, highlighting various initiatives concerning student accommodation, transportation, healthcare, skills development, facilities for female students, research and academic activities.
The report also acknowledged that several initiatives remain under implementation, while a number of projects have been stalled due to administrative complications and other reasons.
Ducsu Vice-President (VP) Abu Shadik Kayem presented the activity and accountability report at a program in front of the Ducsu building on Thursday afternoon. Other Ducsu leaders were also present at the program.
Shadik alleged that the university administration has not yet provided the budget allocated for Ducsu.
“Throughout the year, the DU administration treated Ducsu like a stepchild. The administration remained non-cooperative throughout the period,” he claimed.
Despite what he described as “hundreds of instances of non-cooperation,” Ducsu committees carried out various activities during the year, including initiatives related to student accommodation, transportation, food quality in residential halls, health, education, research and publication, he said.
According to the report, Ducsu organized motorcycle and car driving training, basic first-aid training in residential halls and free spoken English courses to enhance students’ skills. It also arranged workshops on research, training on preparing research proposals, sessions on scholarships and higher education, and various programs including education and job fairs.
In the transport sector, the report mentioned the introduction of bus services on Saturdays, evening trips on various routes, dedicated bus services for female residential halls and a weekly Dhaka-Comilla bus service. It also said various initiatives had been taken to modernize the transportation system and expand bus routes.
In healthcare, the report highlighted initiatives to renovate the university’s medical centre, organize medical camps and provide specialized healthcare services.
The report also said an initiative had been taken to renovate the Ducsu building and use it as a skills development center. As part of efforts to facilitate international exposure for students and representatives, it also mentioned visits to various universities and institutions in China.
The report also highlighted the issue of introducing a teacher evaluation system. According to Ducsu, the proposed teacher evaluation system had been raised through the relevant academic process but could not be implemented due to administrative delays. Ducsu later launched a website titled “DU Teachers’ Evaluation” on its own initiative.
A significant portion of the report, however, focused on initiatives that have not yet been implemented or remain stalled. Ducsu attributed some of the delays to a lack of cooperation from the university administration.
Regarding the accommodation crisis, the report mentioned initiatives to construct new residential halls and buildings for students. It also claimed that Ducsu’s proposals concerning the seat allocation policy had not been properly considered.
On campus stability, Shadik claimed that no classes or examinations were suspended during the year due to campus unrest.
Alongside detailing Ducsu’s activities, the report highlighted various obstacles in coordinating with the university administration and initiatives that remain unimplemented. It stressed the need to complete the pending activities in the future.
Calling for the next Ducsu election to be held soon, VP Shadik Kayem said, “We want elected representatives to stand up for the rights of students.”

item.title: Mahdi Amin urges India to prevent fugitives from creating instability
item.description:
Prime Minister’s Adviser and Prime Minister’s Office spokesperson Mahdi Amin has urged Indian High Commissioner to Bangladesh Dinesh Trivedi to ensure that fugitives linked to the previous regime and individuals convicted by Bangladeshi courts who are currently in India do not attempt to create instability.
Trivedi paid a courtesy call on Mahdi Amin at the Prime Minister’s Office in Tejgaon on Thursday morning.
The meeting focused on strengthening bilateral relations and people-to-people ties between Bangladesh and India. Indian Deputy High Commissioner Pawan Badhe was also present.
The two sides discussed the importance of consolidating democratic values and agreed on the need to take bilateral relations forward based on mutual respect, equality, fairness and justice.
They also discussed resolving existing challenges through dialogue and cooperation.
The meeting covered various aspects of Bangladesh-India relations, with particular emphasis on cooperation in education, health, sports, culture and tourism.
The two sides also discussed expanding trade, business and investment, as well as opportunities for greater cooperation in information technology, innovation, science and technology.

item.title: BDR mutiny: Four allegedly shot, dumped in river
item.description:
Four people, including a witness to the BDR killings, were allegedly blindfolded, shot and dumped into the Baleshwar River in 2010, Major (retd) Md Sabbir Rahman Osmani told the International Crimes Tribunal on Thursday.
He gave the testimony on Thursday before International Crimes Tribunal-1 in a case concerning allegations of enforced disappearance.
Sabbir testified that members of the intelligence wing of RAB-8 carried out the killings in May 2010 in the presence and under the orders of Ziaul Ahsan, who was then head of the RAB intelligence wing.
He said the four people were taken on a fishing trawler to the Baleshwar River near Charduani in Patharghata. Their faces and bodies were covered before they were allegedly shot.
According to his testimony, the victims’ abdomens were then slit open and cement sacks were tied to their bodies before they were thrown into the river.
Sabbir further testified that another person was killed and dumped in the river in 2010 using the same method.
He also said Alkas Majhi, a boatman whose trawler was allegedly used in Ziaul Ahsan’s “Golf Operation” in 2011, was forcibly disappeared and killed.
Former army chief Iqbal Karim Bhuiyan, along with army officers and RAB officials who allegedly witnessed the killings, has already testified against Ziaul Ahsan in the enforced disappearance case.
The testimony of the investigating officer will now be recorded, after which the case will move to the final stage with the presentation of arguments.

item.title: EC suspends ‘Boat’ symbol, introduces ‘No’ option for solo candidates
item.description:
The Election Commission (EC) has amended the Election Conduct Rules, 2008, for the upcoming parliamentary election, suspending the "Boat" symbol and introducing a "No" symbol for constituencies where there is only one candidate.
The EC issued a gazette notification on the amendment from its secretariat on Wednesday.
Under the amended Rule 9(1), a contesting candidate can be allocated any available symbol from the prescribed list, except those marked as suspended.
The EC’s list includes symbols such as pineapple, apple, mango, eagle, camel, cow, rose, bell, kite, truck, tractor, book, bicycle, tiger, rocket, rickshaw, plough, scissors, axe, horse, spectacles, umbrella and jug.
It also includes ship, torch, table, table clock, telephone, television, lock, weighing scales, sheaf of paddy, anchor, palanquin, butterfly, football, cauliflower, bucket, electric fan, light bulb, ladder, mug, peacock, torch, microphone, fish, car, motorcycle, mobile phone, rooster, lion, sunflower, sewing machine, deer, duck, hand, wristwatch, elephant, hammer, hurricane lamp, helicopter and handshake.
The "Boat" symbol is explicitly marked as “suspended” on the list.
The revised rules were issued under Article 94 of the Representation of the People Order, 1972.

item.title: Bangladesh seeks greater French investment in sectors
item.description:
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir on Thursday encouraged greater French investment in Bangladesh and highlighted the potential for enhanced cooperation in promising sectors, including infrastructure, renewable energy, space, technology and pharmaceuticals.
He also underscored the importance of creating greater opportunities for legal and regular labour mobility between Bangladesh and France.
The issues were discussed when Ambassador of France to Bangladesh Jean-Marc Séré-Charlet paid a courtesy call on the state minister at the ministry.
The state minister reaffirmed Bangladesh’s zero-tolerance policy towards irregular migration and human trafficking and expressed Bangladesh’s readiness to work closely with France in addressing these challenges.
The ambassador congratulated the state minister on his assumption of office and exchanged views on ways to further strengthen the longstanding friendship and partnership between Bangladesh and France.
The state minister appreciated France’s continued engagement with Bangladesh, including its support for Bangladesh’s socio-economic development, democratic transition and institutional strengthening.
He emphasised Bangladesh’s interest in further engagment in areas of mutual interest, particularly trade and investment, defence, aviation, education, culture, and human capital development.
They also exchanged views on the priorities and expectations from the upcoming United Nations General Assembly (UNGA).
Both sides also discussed on regional and global issues, including climate change and multilateral engagement reiterating their commitment to working together in international fora.
Ambassador Séré-Charlet reaffirmed France’s readiness to enhance cooperation across all areas of mutual interest. He appreciated the Government’s efforts towards democratic reforms and expressed France’s interest in working closely with Bangladesh.
Humaiun Kobir appreciated the France’s continued humanitarian support for the 1.3 million Rohingyas sheltered in Bangladesh.
Both sides also expressed their readiness to work together for their safe, voluntary and dignified repatriation.
Both sides expressed confidence that continued engagement and enhanced cooperation would provide further momentum to Bangladesh-France relations.

item.title: Law minister: Government committed to protecting citizens’ rights
item.description:
Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs Minister Md Asaduzzaman has said the government is committed to protecting the rights of citizens under all circumstances.
He made the remarks at a national consultation meeting held at Hotel InterContinental in Dhaka on Thursday on strengthening the criminal justice system’s response to human trafficking and migrant smuggling.
The meeting was organized by the Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs and the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC).
Describing human trafficking as one of the most serious and inhumane crimes, the law minister said fraudsters, criminals and mafia groups make large sums of money through the exploitation of human lives.
“The government is committed to changing this situation,” he said.
Highlighting amendments to laws aimed at curbing human trafficking, Md Asaduzzaman said: “We have amended several laws. We have made the definition of human trafficking more realistic so that it can be applied to a wider range of trafficking activities. We have incorporated such provisions under the Human Trafficking Prevention Act.”
“We amended the Gambling Act of 1887 to bring online gambling, trafficking and similar illegal activities under our legal framework. Additionally, we have introduced other laws that also cover aspects of human trafficking,” he added.
The law minister said Bangladesh ratified the protocol on human trafficking in September 2019 and has since been working to fulfil its commitments to the international community.
Acknowledging some limitations faced by law enforcement agencies, he said: “Our law enforcement agencies are quite vigilant. However, they face constraints regarding manpower, adequate cooperation from complainants, and the acquisition of suitable evidence and other necessary elements.”
He said human trafficking was no longer as widespread as it had been in the past, noting that Bangladesh also faces an unemployment crisis and cannot prevent people from travelling abroad in search of livelihoods.
“It must be acknowledged that human trafficking is not as widespread now as it used to be. You must remember that our country faces an unemployment crisis; we cannot prevent people from going abroad in search of a livelihood,” he said.
Noting that many people become undocumented migrants after travelling abroad on tourist visas, he sought assistance in ensuring the rights of Bangladeshis travelling overseas.
“In this context, we are seeking your assistance on how to ensure the rights of migrants travelling abroad,” he said.
Reiterating the government’s commitment to protecting citizens’ rights, Md Asaduzzaman said: “We are committed to safeguarding the rights of our citizens under any circumstances. We may have some shortcomings, but we welcome any constructive recommendations you may have.”
UNODC Regional Representative for South Asia Christian Holge attended the event as a special guest.
The meeting was presided over by Md Khademul Kayes, additional secretary of the Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs.

item.title: Study: 59% of measles infections occurred in healthcare facilities
item.description:
A study has found that 59.4% of children hospitalised with measles in Chittagong, Comilla and Cox’s Bazar contracted the virus at healthcare facilities, highlighting significant gaps in infection prevention and control measures at hospitals.
The findings were presented in the conference room of Chittagong Medical College on Wednesday.
The study, titled “Measles Outbreak in Southern Bangladesh: Disease Spread, Symptoms, Genetic Analysis, and Maternal-Child Antibody Status,” was conducted by the Asperia Health Research and Development Foundation (AHRDF).
The study showed that of 200 children hospitalised with measles in Chittagong, Comilla and Cox’s Bazar, 167 had not been vaccinated against the disease.
However, 91 of the unvaccinated children had not yet reached the age for routine measles vaccination.
Genome sequencing of samples from 17 infected children identified the B3 genotype in all cases, a strain that can be controlled through vaccination.
Malnutrition emerged as a major underlying factor in severe illness, with 31% of the affected children suffering from severe malnutrition.
Researchers collected data from 200 children treated for measles and 100 of their mothers at Chittagong Medical College Hospital, Mother and Child Hospital, Comilla Medical College Hospital and Cox’s Bazar Medical College Hospital.
Kamrun Nahar, associate professor of child health at Chittagong Medical College, was the principal investigator.
Among the 200 children, 46% were under nine months old, meaning they contracted measles before reaching the routine vaccination age.
Of the infected children, 148 (75.5%) were from rural areas, while 127 (64.8%) belonged to low-income families.
“A significant portion of the outbreak is linked to rural areas, demonstrating that poor and marginalised populations are at extreme risk from this virus,” Kamrun Nahar said.
The study found that malnutrition was a major factor contributing to severe disease and measles-related complications.
About 31% of the children were suffering from severe malnutrition. The study also found that 18.9% were fed foods other than breast milk, which the researchers said could compromise their immune systems.
The report noted that Vitamin A can help prevent severe complications from measles. However, only 63 children (32%) had received Vitamin A capsules during the previous six months, indicating a significant gap in coverage.
“Among the children who did not receive Vitamin A, 59% developed severe and acute complications,” Kamrun Nahar said.
She added that exclusive breastfeeding alone was insufficient to reduce the severity of measles and that other medical interventions and proper nutrition were essential.
The study found that moderate to severe malnutrition, living in rural areas or slums, poverty, overcrowded housing and Vitamin A deficiency were associated with a higher risk of severe complications.
Among children whose mothers had no history of measles vaccination, 55% suffered severe complications after contracting the disease.
Of the 200 measles patients, 167 had not been vaccinated. However, 91 of them had not yet reached the eligible age for routine vaccination.
Overall, the patients ranged in age from two months to 11 years, with 46% under nine months old.
In Bangladesh, the first routine measles vaccination is administered at nine months, meaning many of these children contracted the disease before becoming eligible for vaccination.
Among unvaccinated children, 52% missed vaccination because of a lack of awareness or forgetting the date, 30% because of illness, 8% because of their mother’s illness, 4% because of fear of vaccination and 4% because they had lost their vaccination cards.
The study found that 59.4% of the infected children contracted measles at healthcare centres or hospitals, highlighting weaknesses in infection prevention and control measures.
“Measles transmission is occurring because multiple children share the same bed due to a shortage of hospital beds,” Kamrun Nahar said.
Professor Dr Mohammad Musa Mia, head of the Department of Paediatrics at Chittagong Medical College Hospital, said patients often remain in general wards while showing symptoms before being diagnosed.
“Transmission occurs among other patients through contact with them. Other patients recover and go home, only to return to the hospital later with measles,” he said.
“If a separate hospital were established for measles, transmission would decrease, and providing treatment would become easier,” he added.
Professor Dr M A Hasan Chowdhury, former head of the Department of Medicine at Chittagong Medical College, said measles was highly contagious and that one patient could infect 12 to 15 others.
“Therefore, isolation is crucial. If infected individuals are not kept separate, the infection spreads rapidly. Health protocols must be strictly followed to prevent transmission,” he said.
The study also found that 32 children, or 16%, had previously come into contact with a measles patient.
According to Kamrun Nahar, 86% of the children who participated in the study recovered and returned home.
The research team conducted genome sequencing on samples from 17 patients and identified the B3 genotype in every case.
Kamrun Nahar said there had been concerns that a new genotype might be circulating because of the presence of Rohingya populations in the region.
“However, the study did not detect any new imported infection,” she said.
She said the B3 genotype had also been identified in tests conducted by the Institute of Epidemiology, Disease Control and Research (IEDCR) and icddr,b.
“This confirms that the current measles outbreak is due to a decline in overall vaccination coverage. Achieving 95% vaccination coverage would make it possible to control the disease,” she said.
Kamrun Nahar said unvaccinated children were nearly twice as likely to develop severe complications as vaccinated children.
“The most reassuring and significant finding is that not a single vaccinated child died,” she said.
The research team recommended regular vaccination campaigns to reach 95% of children, door-to-door vaccination for children who missed their doses, Vitamin A supplementation, improved child nutrition, rapid detection and isolation of children below the eligible vaccination age, and adequate isolation facilities and proper ventilation in hospitals.
Brigadier General Mohammad Taslim Uddin, director of Chittagong Medical College Hospital, said the level of isolation used during the Covid-19 pandemic was not being maintained for measles patients.
“If strict isolation is implemented and 95% of children are vaccinated, control will be possible,” he said.
He said 193 measles patients were currently admitted to the hospital and the number was continuing to rise.
“Transmission is also occurring within the hospital from infected patients to others,” he said.
Speaking at the event, Chittagong City Corporation Mayor Shahadat Hossain attributed the situation to the failure to hold the 2024 vaccination campaign and shortcomings over the past few years.
“Both vaccination and isolation must be ensured. Why are there so many patients despite vaccinating more children than the target?” he said.
“Since measles is highly contagious, isolation is the primary priority now. The nutritional needs of the children’s mothers must also be ensured,” he added.
Recommendations were also made at the event to maintain year-round vaccination programs, strictly enforce isolation protocols and consider establishing a dedicated measles treatment facility in Chittagong to help curb transmission.

item.title: PM accords reception to winners of international Quran competition
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Thursday accorded a reception to four Bangladeshi Hafizs who won prizes at the 46th King Abdulaziz International Quran Competition held in Saudi Arabia, saying the government will recognise the achievements of citizens who excel through their merit and ability.
“You have not only brought this achievement for yourselves. I believe it is an achievement of all Muslims in Bangladesh,” the prime minister said while speaking at a reception for the prize-winning Hafizs at the Cabinet Division conference room at the Bangladesh Secretariat.
Congratulating the winners, he also said it was the government’s policy to recognise the achievements of talented citizens.
“Almost all of you have mentioned that Hafizs have been encouraged and honoured after a long time. This is a policy of the present government that when the children of the country, who are the future of the country, achieve something good through their ability and merit, the government will try to recognise that achievement from the state’s position,” Tarique said.
He said encouraging talented people and properly assessing their merit would certainly benefit future generations and the country.
Tarique said the government has been trying to encourage talented and qualified people since taking office, and inviting the prize-winning Hafizs to the reception was part of that effort.
Teachers of the prize-winning Hafizs raised some of their problems with the Prime Minister.
Tarique said he would discuss the issues with the relevant minister and explore possible solutions.
“You have mentioned some problems. We will see, InshaAllah, whether there is any way to solve them and, if so, what that way is. We will certainly try to do whatever is possible from our side,” he said.
The prime minister also assured them of government support for participation in future international competitions.
“There may be more such competitions ahead. If government support is needed to participate in such competitions in the future, you will inform us through the proper channels. We will take whatever measures are possible from the government’s side,” he said.
Tarique said he wanted Bangladeshi boys and girls to participate in such international competitions and bring honour and glory to themselves, the country and its people.
Calling for collective efforts to establish peace and bring positive changes to the country, he said people might have different ways of working, but their goal was the same.
“That is to establish peace in the country so that everyone can live well and peacefully together. So that people can live like human beings. That is our effort, that is our initiative,” Tarique said.
Seeking everyone’s cooperation and prayers for the government, he said: “We want to work for the country and its people. We want to move forward together with everyone. We want to bring positive changes to the country together with everyone.”
The prime minister gifted books to the winners at the programme. Earlier, he listened to the Hafizs recite verses from the surahs through which they won prizes in the competition.
Among competitors from 133 countries, Hafiz Mohammad Zakaria of Bangladesh won first place in the 15-para Hifz, Tajweed and beautiful recitation category.
Hafiz Sheikh Mohammad Mahmudul Hasan Ashrafi secured third place in the 30-para Hifz, Tajweed and beautiful recitation category.
Hafiza Rabeta Binte Ramzan and Hafiza Musfira Binte Mahmud also secured third place in the 15-para and 30-para Hifz, Tajweed and beautiful recitation categories respectively.
Religious Affairs Minister Kazi Shah Mofazzal Houssain Kaikobad, State Minister Shamim Kaiser, Cabinet Secretary Nasimul Ghani and Principal Secretary to the Prime Minister ABM Abdus Sattar were present, among others.
Teachers of the prize-winning Hafizs — Qayum Molla, Muinuddeen Majumder, Abu Bakar, Sajeda Khatun and Maulana Rafiqul Islam — were also present.

item.title: Gas, electricity supply improve slightly in Savar industrial zone
item.description:
Gas and electricity supplies have improved slightly in industrial and residential areas of Savar, Ashulia and Dhamrai, bringing some relief to factories and households after days of shortages.
The improvement has allowed some factories to resume boiler and ironing operations, although gas pressure remains well below the level required for normal production, according to officials and industry representatives.
Sources at the Savar regional office of Titas Gas Transmission and Distribution Company Limited and Dhaka Palli Bidyut Samity-1 confirmed the improvement.
On Wednesday, visits to factories in Savar, Ashulia and Dhamrai found that gas pressure had increased slightly from the levels recorded in recent days.
There are around 1,200 factories in the Savar-Ashulia industrial zone. Industry representatives said gas supply had increased particularly in factories where boiler and ironing sections are operational.
Factories generally require gas pressure of 10-15 PSI for normal production. In recent days, pressure had dropped to zero in some areas. Since Wednesday, however, supply has been available at around 2-3 PSI.
The situation was observed in areas including Radio Colony and Hemayetpur in Savar, and Jamgora, Kathgora, Jirabo, Narsinghapur, Berun, Shimultala, Palashbari, Nishchintapur, Baipail and Jirani in Ashulia.
Mortuz Ali, a director of a garment factory in Savar, said the factory had been unable to operate its boilers and ironing sections for several days.
“We couldn’t operate our boilers or ironing sections for the past few days. However, gas supply has increased since yesterday. We are able to do some work today, although the supply remains insufficient; it needs to be increased further,” he said.
Habibur Rahman, general manager of a garment factory in Dhamrai, said the increased supply had allowed limited production.
“The increase allows for limited work. Still, it is better than having almost no supply at all,” he said.
Gas pressure has also increased slightly in residential areas, although residents said supplies remained inadequate for cooking.
Ferdousi Sultana, a resident of Radio Colony in Savar, said there had been no gas for nearly two months.
“There was absolutely no gas for nearly two months. Now, however, some is coming through. But the supply we are getting makes cooking difficult,” she said.
Many residents have turned to alternative cooking arrangements amid the shortage.
Sharmin Akter, a resident of College Road in Savar Municipality, said: “We aren’t getting gas at any time—day or night. So, I’ve brought in a cylinder and am cooking with that.”
Engineer Abu Saleh Muhammad Khademuddin, official in charge of the Titas Gas Ashulia Zone, said the situation had improved slightly since Wednesday.
“The situation has improved slightly since yesterday. Supply has risen from zero to 2-3 PSI. We expect the situation to improve further in the coming days,” he said.
Mohammad Mominul Islam Bhuiyan, superintendent of Industrial Police-1, which covers Savar and Ashulia, said he had learned that gas supply had increased.
“There are no reports of factories halting operations or facing issues due to the gas crisis,” he said.
Mohiuddin Rubel, founder and CEO of Bangladesh Apparel Voice and a former director of the BGMEA, said gas supply had improved and was returning roughly to its previous level.
“We expect the situation to improve further in line with the government’s assurances. In particular, there is no alternative to increasing supply to factories to sustain the industry,” he said.
The electricity situation has also improved slightly, although several grids continue to face supply deficits.
According to Palli Bidyut data, electricity demand at the Savar grid at 2pm Wednesday was 42MW, against a supply of 37MW, resulting in 5MW of load-shedding.
At the Nabinagar grid, demand was 90MW and supply was 78MW, resulting in 12MW of load-shedding.
At the Dhamrai grid, demand and supply were both 11MW, while both stood at 3MW at the Mirzapur grid. According to National Load Dispatch Centre (NLDC) figures, there was no load-shedding at either grid.
At the Kabirpur grid, demand was 250MW against a supply of 210MW, leaving a 40MW deficit.
At the Kadda grid, demand stood at 110MW against a supply of 75MW. NLDC-imposed load-shedding accounted for 15MW, while feeder shutdowns caused by bus overloading accounted for another 20MW.
Supply from the Summit power plant was 9MW, while United Power supplied no electricity, according to the data.
The total electricity demand in the area served by Dhaka Palli Bidyut Samity-1 was 515MW against a supply of 423MW. Total NLDC load-shedding was 72MW, while overloading accounted for another 20MW.
Md Akteruzzaman Laskar, senior general manager of Dhaka Palli Bidyut Samity-1, said electricity supply had increased compared to previous days.
“Electricity supply has increased compared to the last few days. The situation will improve further. We are striving to distribute electricity based on priority,” he said.

item.title: Major reshuffle, promotions in top police ranks
item.description:
The Bangladesh Police has undergone a major reshuffle, with six officers promoted to Additional Inspector General of Police (Addl IGP) and five Deputy Inspector General (DIG)-rank officers transferred to new positions.
Two separate notifications were issued by the Police-1 Branch of the Public Security Division under the Ministry of Home Affairs on Thursday.
The notifications, issued by order of the president, were signed by Deputy Secretary Tawsif Ahmed.
According to the first notification, Sayedur Rahman, former director (DIG) of Rajarbagh Central Police Hospital, has been promoted to Addl IGP and posted to Police Headquarters.
Mainul Hasan, currently serving as Addl IGP (in-charge) of Tourist Police, has been posted as principal (Addl IGP) of the Sarda Police Academy.
Dhaka Range DIG Iqbal Hossain and Police Headquarters DIG Kamrul Ahsan have been promoted to Addl IGP and posted to Police Headquarters and the Special Branch (SB), respectively.
Special Branch Addl IGP Sardar Nurul Amin has been transferred to Police Headquarters, while Sarda Police Academy Principal GM Azizur Rahman has been transferred as Addl IGP of Tourist Police.
The second notification announced the reshuffle of five DIG-rank officers.
Police Headquarters DIG Rezaul Karim has been transferred as DIG of Khulna Range, while Khulna Range DIG Mostafizur Rahman has been transferred as DIG of Dhaka Range.
Anti-Terrorism Unit DIG Mohammad Muslim has been appointed director of Rajarbagh Central Police Hospital.
SB DIG Mir Ashraf Ali has been transferred as DIG of Railway Police, while Mass Rapid Transit (Metro Rail) DIG Siddiqui Tanjilur Rahman has been appointed DIG of the Special Branch.
The notification said the transfers and postings were made in the public interest and would take effect immediately.

item.title: Australia to cut student, backpacker visas in migration curb
item.description:
Australia will cut migration by toughening visa rules for foreign students, backpackers, and working holiday-makers, the Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke said Thursday.
Under the new rules, foreign students will no longer be allowed to bring partners and children to join them while they study in Australia, while people who overstay their working holiday visas will face tougher enforcement.
The government is also cracking down on so-called “visa hopping,” where foreign migrants who are already in Australia move from one type of temporary visa to another to extend their stay.
“If you want to come on a temporary basis to Australia, apply for a temporary visa. If you want ‌to ​come to Australia permanently, apply for a permanent visa. And if you no longer have a valid visa, you should leave Australia,” Burke said.
What else did the Home Affairs Minister say about the migration reforms?
In remarks to the National Press Club in Canberra on Thursday, Burke insisted that immigration remains “fundamentally a strength” for Australia, but acknowledged that rules needed adjusting to ease pressure on housing.
“We need immigration to soften enough that housing has a chance to catch up,” he said, while stressing the housing shortage was not caused by migrants.
Burke said it was “simply demonstrably wrong” that his ruling center-left Labor party was beefing up its visa rules as a response to a surge in the polls by the far-right One Nation.
This year, the group has become one of the country’s most popular parties, campaigning on pledges to slash migration to the country as part of its “Australia First” approach, which has drawn similarities to US President Donald Trump.
The hard-right party said this week that it would cut the number of temporary migrants by 750,000 over the next three years to give Australians “breathing space.”
The cost of living and immigration have ranked as some of voters’ most pressing concerns in recent polls.
The changes are set to see net annual migration fall from the current 300,000 to around 225,000 by 2028. That would see numbers return to the levels before the Covid-19 pandemic.
Annual migration surged to its highest level of 538,000 in 2022, after borders reopened.
Data on Thursday showed that migration numbers had declined to 292,100 in the year to March, 47% below the peak following the pandemic, Burke said.
Students make up the biggest immigrant group: some 753,000 foreign students live in Australia, most of whom come from China and India.
The reforms will see Australia return to its policy of a decade earlier when those who overstayed were given two weeks to leave the country or face detention and deportation, the minister said.
People seeking to extend their working holiday visas in rural areas will enter a ballot for a second or third year.
Applicants with skills in construction and housing will be prioritized for visas, Burke said.
Relatives of visa holders wanting to visit the country will have “no further stay” conditions applied to their visas.

item.title: Trump threatens EU with further sanctions over Canada
item.description:
US President Donald Trump on Wednesday responded to the European Union’s plans to add Canada as an associate member with threats and ridicule.
During her annual speech at the European Parliament in Strasbourg, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said the EU was opening the door for ‌Canada ⁠to ⁠become its first associate member.
Such a relationship to the bloc does not currently exist and would have to be created from scratch.
In comments to reporters on Wednesday, Trump said the idea could become a “hostile act.” He threatened to impose sanctions on the EU in response.
“If they do that, if I think it’s at all a hostile act, I will put very serious tariffs or stop trading with Europe on many things,” Trump told reporters en route to an event in North Carolina.
The US president also described the prospect of Canada joining the EU as “laughable.”
The potential Canadian EU associate membership comes as Trump, during his second term in office, has shaken Washington’s relationship with its northern neighbor to the core.
Canada was among the first victims of Trump’s tariff policy.
Tensions escalated between Ottawa and Washington after trade talks broke down last month, with Trump imposing further sanctions on Canada and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney vowing to respond in kind.
Washington’s transatlantic ties have also suffered under Trump, most notably after the US president’s push to take control of the Arctic island of Greenland, which is part of the Kingdom of Denmark.
The EU was also hit by Trump’s wide tariffs, as were most countries worldwide, but the two sides reached a trade agreement to bring them down.

item.title: bKash achieves gold at ESG Excellence Awards 2026
item.description:
bKash has won the Gold Award in the ‘Excellence in Sustainable Product Innovation’ category at the ESG Excellence Awards 2026 for its green financial initiatives.
Maj Gen Sheikh Md Monirul Islam (retd), chief external and corporate affairs officer of bKash, received the accolade at a city hotel.
Environment, Forest and Climate Change Minister Abdul Awal Mintoo attended the event as chief guest.
The event brought together senior government officials, diplomats - including heads of missions from the EU, Denmark, Sweden, and Australia - and business leaders.
Jointly organized by the ESG Institute Bangladesh and the UN Global Compact Network Bangladesh, the awards recognize organizations demonstrating excellence in environmental, social, and governance (ESG) practices.
bKash was honoured for embedding environmental responsibility and social empowerment into its core digital financial ecosystem.
bKash has been saving approximately 1,200 metric tonnes of paper annually from its 1.5 billion digital transactions conducted through the platform.
The shift towards mobile financial services has also significantly reduced customer travel to physical outlets, cutting transport-related carbon emissions.
Beyond environmental benefits, bKash’s digital financial ecosystem supports broader socioeconomic development.
Its platform contributes to financial inclusion, women’s economic empowerment, digital salary disbursements, government-to-person payments, humanitarian assistance, remittances, and access to formal financial products.
The award submission indicates that bKash has facilitated financial aid to approximately 14 million beneficiaries, while its digital financial services have also helped expand access to savings and formal credit.
Maj Gen Sheikh Md Monirul Islam (retd), chief external and corporate affairs officer of bKash, said: “At bKash, we view ESG not as a separate agenda, but as an integral part of how we innovate, grow, and create value. This recognition is particularly meaningful as it acknowledges how digital financial innovation can create shared value - advancing financial inclusion and economic empowerment while contributing to environmental sustainability. We appreciate the ESG Institute Bangladesh and the UN Global Compact Network Bangladesh for this recognition, which inspires us to keep innovating responsibly for a more inclusive, digitally connected, and sustainable Bangladesh.”
Looking ahead, bKash is also exploring tech-enabled afforestation initiatives that connect customer transaction milestones with tree planting and nurturing.
The inaugural edition of this award recognized the ESG contribution of 32 companies and three individuals.
Awards were presented across 20 categories, including energy transition, water stewardship, carbon emission control, occupational health and safety, worker wellbeing, skills development, gender equity, supply chain management, sustainability reporting, and product and digital innovation.

item.title: Former CTTC ADC among 5 charged over enforced disappearance, murder
item.description:
The prosecution has filed formal charges against five people, including former Counter Terrorism and Transnational Crime (CTTC) additional deputy commissioner Ishtiaq Ahmed, over allegations of enforced disappearance and murder.
Ishtiaq, who is currently in jail, is accused of abducting Maulana Al Amin, keeping him in detention for an extended period and later killing him, Chief Prosecutor Md Aminul Islam said at a briefing at the International Crimes Tribunal on Wednesday.
The prosecution filed the formal charges with the tribunal after the investigation agency submitted its report.
Prosecutor Gazi Monawar Hossain Tamim alleged that the CTTC abducted religious-minded youths for criticising the government or posting against it on social media.
“They would be forcibly disappeared and detained in various Aynaghar [secret detention facilities]. When a government decision came, they would be taken to a specific location and killed in staged militant incidents,” he said.
Gazi Monawar also said that in some cases, the bodies were made to disappear, while others were sent to court in false cases.
He said the formal charges against the five accused were filed in connection with one such case.

item.title: 12 APBn recovers 3,165 lost, stolen phones in 22 months
item.description:
The 12 Armed Police Battalion (APBn) has recovered 3,165 mobile phones of various brands by using information technology to track lost and stolen devices over the past 22 months.
The phones were recovered after investigating around 14,322 general diaries (GDs) filed at different police stations, according to a press release issued by 12 APBn on Wednesday.
After verification, the recovered phones were handed over to their rightful owners.
The 12 APBn has a cyber and Call Detail Record (CDR) analysis unit dedicated to recovering lost mobile phones. The unit collects GDs filed at police stations across Bangladesh and uses information technology to track the devices.
The battalion said it also collects information about lost phones from relatives, friends and acquaintances. Investigators then use details in the GDs and the phones’ International Mobile Equipment Identity (IMEI) numbers to trace them.
The 12 APBn has ranked first among all APBn battalions in recovering lost mobile phones for the past 21 months, the release said. It recovered 132 lost phones in August alone.
The 12 APBn advised mobile phone users to keep a record of their phone’s International Mobile Equipment Identity (IMEI) number after purchase. The 15-digit number is usually printed on the phone’s box and is required if the device is lost or stolen.
If a phone is lost, users should file an online GD with the relevant police station, mentioning the IMEI number.
A copy of the GD can then be sent to 12 APBn through its designated WhatsApp numbers, 01320-194018 and 01320-194003. A copy can also be sent through the 12 APBn Facebook page.
The battalion said its cyber team is working to recover the phones under the overall supervision of 12 APBn Commanding Officer Additional DIG Md Enamul Kabir and the leadership of Additional Superintendent of Police (Operations and Intelligence) Md Saiful Islam.

item.title: Four policemen arrested at gambling spot in Thakurgaon
item.description:
Four police personnel were arrested from a gambling spot in an abandoned tin-shed building near the office of the superintendent of police (SP) of Thakurgaon early Tuesday.
The arrestees are Assistant Sub-Inspectors (ASI) Md Shahadat Zaman, 39, and Shanti Kumar Roy, 37, and constables Md Sohel Rana, 33, and Alamgir Kabir, 33.
The latter three were serving at the Thakurgaon SP office, while the former was posted at Sadar Police Outpost.
Two others who were allegedly involved in the gambling fled the scene during the raid. They are Panchagarh district police Assistant Traffic SI Md Ataur Rahman, 40, and Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI) Thakurgaon constable Md Shahidul Islam, 38.
Police said they raided the den at Holpara around 1:30am following a tip-off.
Those present tried to leave after sensing the presence of the law enforcers, leading to a scuffle as police tried to stop them.
Additional SP (Sadar Circle) Jewel Rana was injured during the incident, according to police.
Police seized playing cards, cash and several smartphones from the spot, along with four motorcycles nearby.
A case was filed with Sadar Police Station in this regard.
Additional SP (Administration and Finance) Md Khodadad Hossain said police have been conducting regular drives against drugs and gambling.
“We had been receiving information for several days that some of our police personnel had become involved in gambling. While verifying the information, they were caught red-handed,” he said.
He said the same legal action will be taken against the police personnel as against ordinary offenders.

item.title: Another train planned on Dhaka–Cox’s Bazar route
item.description:
Bangladesh Railway plans to extend the Mahanagar Express, currently operating between Dhaka and Chittagong , to Cox’s Bazar to meet growing demand for rail travel.
If preparations are completed on schedule, the service could begin operating on the Dhaka–Cox’s Bazar route in the first week of October, railway officials said.
Sujit Biswas, chief commercial manager of Bangladesh Railway’s Eastern Zone, said the route had proved profitable, with existing trains frequently operating at full capacity.
Demand for tickets remains high, prompting authorities to increase train services from both Dhaka and Chittagong to Cox’s Bazar, he said.
Mahanagar Express currently leaves Kamalapur Railway Station at 9:20 p.m. for Chittagong and arrives at around 3:30 a.m. The train stops at 12 stations, including Dhaka Airport, Narsingdi, Bhairab Bazar, Ashuganj, Brahmanbaria, Akhaura, Kasba, Cumilla, Laksham, Nangalkot, Feni and Kumira.
Under the proposed extension, train numbers 721 and 722 would leave Kamalapur at around 8:30 p.m. and reach Cox’s Bazar at about 6 a.m. The return service would depart Cox’s Bazar at 9 a.m. and arrive in Dhaka around 6:30 p.m.
The extension would provide passengers from Dhaka, Chittagong and several intermediate stations with a direct rail link to Cox’s Bazar.
The move is part of Bangladesh Railway’s broader plan to expand services on the Dhaka–Chittagong –Cox’s Bazar corridor. Four pairs of trains currently operate to Cox’s Bazar from Dhaka and Chittagong, with plans to increase the number to five pairs.
Commercial train services on the Dhaka–Cox’s Bazar route began on Dec. 1, 2023.
Shafikur Rahman, chief operating superintendent of Bangladesh Railway’s Eastern Zone, said preparations were underway and the new service could begin next month.

item.title: 180-day review finds gaps in govt action on women, children’s rights
item.description:
A review of the government’s first 180 days has found gaps in implementing its election manifesto commitments on women’s and children’s rights, with speakers calling for stronger political commitment, clearer implementation plans and regular accountability.
The review identified shortcomings in implementation planning, prevention of child marriage and child labor, health financing, inclusive water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH), protection of marginalized groups and regular accountability.
At the same time, progress was noted in areas including budget allocations, school feeding, health service initiatives, expansion of one-stop crisis centers and disability allowance measures.
The findings were presented at a discussion titled “From Commitment to Implementation: The Government’s 180 Days in Protecting the Rights of Women and Children,” organized by the Coalition for Advancing Equality and Justice at Hotel Lakeshore in Gulshan on Wednesday.
The review covered five areas: education; health and nutrition; protection from violence; climate risk and WASH; and diversity and inclusion.
Presenting the keynote, Wasiur Rahman Tonmoy, Lead for Youth and Social Cohesion at Manusher Jonno Foundation, and Rowshon Akhter Urmee, Gender Justice and Social Inclusion Specialist at Oxfam in Bangladesh, outlined the progress and gaps identified in the review.
They recommended faster action on an anti-discrimination law, stronger measures to prevent child marriage and child labor, curriculum reform, health insurance, inclusive WASH systems, manifesto-based budgeting and regular reviews of progress.
Opening the discussion on behalf of the coalition, Kabita Bose, Country Director of Plan International Bangladesh, said the coalition was formed by seven national and international organizations ahead of the 13th National Parliamentary Election to bring women’s and children’s rights more prominently into political and development discussions.
The coalition had submitted evidence-based recommendations to 14 political parties, she said, noting that women, children, girls and young people often receive less priority in election manifestos.
“Investment in women and children should not be seen as charity, but as a rights-based and strategic development priority,” Bose said.
She said the coalition wanted to work with the government and other stakeholders to review progress, identify gaps and support implementation of the commitments.
Political representation
During the panel discussion, BNP reserved-seat MP Anna Minj said women elected through reserved seats were active and capable, but their direct political representation remained constrained by party structures, nomination barriers, election costs and online harassment.
She said the 33% target for women’s participation had not yet been fully implemented and argued that meaningful inclusion should begin within political parties through greater representation of women and other marginalized groups.
Dr Nazneen Ahmed, Executive Director of the Centre for Policy Dialogue, identified financial capacity, priority setting and governance as key challenges.
“Women need equity, not just equality, because years of policy gaps have kept them behind,” she said.
Nazneen also called for initiatives such as the Pink Bus service to be reviewed after several months to determine whether they were reducing harassment or creating new barriers for women.
Dr Md Shafiqul Islam Masud, Jamaat-e-Islami MP from Patuakhali-2, said women’s and children’s rights required political unity, safe workplaces, improved healthcare, childcare support and faster access to justice.
Many incidents of violence may remain unreported because victims fear retaliation or cannot afford legal action, he said, calling on political parties to take a zero-tolerance position on violence against women and children.
Nusrat Tabassum Jyoti, a reserved-seat MP from the National Citizens Party, said women and children continued to face insecurity at home, in public spaces, online and while seeking justice.
She stressed the need to ensure nutritious food for women and girls from childhood and called for stronger protection against violence, clearer safeguards in cyber laws and measures to address deepfake-based abuse.
Climate vulnerability
Md Shamsuddoha, Chief Executive of the Centre for Participatory Research and Development, said climate change was affecting women and children beyond the immediate impacts of cyclones, river erosion and heatwaves.
He pointed to waterlogging, crop losses, migration, child labor, school dropout and poverty as interconnected consequences of climate vulnerability.
He called for human-centered climate planning, stronger governance of climate finance and greater integration of climate action into national development planning.
Govt response
Speaking as chief guest, State Minister for Primary and Mass Education Bobby Hajjaj thanked the coalition for reviewing manifesto commitments and maintaining public scrutiny of political pledges.
He said democratic politics should be based on merit, public service and people’s trust rather than muscle power.
“We must stop dividing ourselves and work together to build a society where women are recognized not only by family roles of being someone’s daughter, mother or wife, but by their own identity and contribution,” Hajjaj said.
He also said temporary measures such as reserved parliamentary seats and Pink Bus services might remain necessary until equal rights and opportunities were ensured.
However, the ultimate goal should be a society where women could participate safely, directly and with dignity, he said.
Hajjaj said the Ministry of Primary and Mass Education was working to strengthen monitoring of primary schools, madrasas and other educational institutions.
The ministry was also planning to pilot free sanitary supplies and awareness programs for adolescent girls and support education infrastructure in haor and other remote areas, he added.
Anil Pant, Country Director of Oxfam in Bangladesh, delivered the vote of thanks.
The Coalition for Advancing Equality and Justice comprises Breaking the Silence, JAAGO Foundation, Manusher Jonno Foundation, Oxfam in Bangladesh, Plan International Bangladesh, Save the Children in Bangladesh and WaterAid Bangladesh.

item.title: Dengue: Seven more die as 1,753 hospitalized in 24 hours
item.description:
Seven more people died of dengue, and 1,753 new patients were hospitalized across the country in 24 hours until 8am on Wednesday.
With the latest fatalities, the dengue death toll has risen to 171 in the country this year, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
Among the deaths, three were reported in Khulna division while one each in Chittagong, Mymensingh, Rajshahi and Rangpur divisions, it said.
Currently, 4,166 dengue patients are undergoing treatment at different hospitals across the country.
Since January 1 this year, a total of 56,916 dengue patients were admitted to hospitals across the country. Of them, 52,579 have recovered.

item.title: ECNEC approves Tk3,822 crore electric train project
item.description:
The government has approved a Tk3,822 crore project to introduce electric train services on the Dhaka-Narayanganj-Joydebpur route by 2031.
The project was among 12 approved by the Executive Committee of the National Economic Council (ECNEC) at a meeting at the Secretariat on Wednesday, chaired by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman.
The 12 projects involve a total cost of Tk168,780 crore and 40 lakh, including three metro rail projects and the electric train project.
Speaking at a press conference in Agargaon after the meeting, Planning State Minister Jonayed Abdur Rahim Saki said the government plans to expand metro rail services in Dhaka and its surrounding areas, as well as in different regions of the country, to improve the transportation system.
He said project costs have increased due to the devaluation of the dollar.
“If project work is not completed quickly, the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) will change the interest rate on its loans after September,” he said.
Alongside the electric train project, three major metro rail projects were revised or newly approved at the ECNEC meeting.
The projects are Metro Rail Line-5 Southern Route, Metro Rail Line-1 and Metro Rail Line-5 Northern Route.
The total cost of implementing the three projects will be around Tk250,000 crore, according to relevant sources.
Revised cost proposals have been made for MRT Line-1, covering the Airport-Kamalapur route, and MRT Line-5 Northern, covering Hemayetpur-Bhatara. Both projects are being financed by JICA.
Meanwhile, the new MRT Line-5 Southern project, covering Gabtoli-Dasherkandi, received approval. The project will be jointly financed by the Asian Development Bank (ADB) and South Korea.

Shama Obaed: Efforts to continue until convicts brought back from India
item.description:
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam on Wednesday said Bangladesh will take all necessary legal and diplomatic steps under existing laws to bring back convicted fugitives including former prime minister Sheikh Hasina and those sentenced to death in the latest verdict.
She said the foreign ministry would initiate the required process with the Indian government once it officially receives all necessary documents related to the verdict delivered on Tuesday.
“Look, this is an ongoing process. I should not and do not wish to comment on the legal aspects,” she told reporters at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
The International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) on Tuesday sentenced seven people including Awami League General Secretary Obaidul Quader to death for their roles in suppressing the July 2024 mass uprising through incitement, provocation, attacks and killings.
Regarding the foreign ministry's responsibility, Shama said, “We are taking and will continue to take all necessary steps under existing laws to extradite convicted criminals, including the former prime minister of the fascist government and those sentenced yesterday (Tuesday).”
She said efforts are underway under the extradition treaty to bring back the former home minister, the former prime minister and the killers of martyr Hadi, who are currently detained in India. “Official correspondence is being exchanged,” she said.
“Since the verdict was delivered just yesterday (Tuesday), once we officially receive all the necessary paperwork, we will contact the Indian government through due process to take whatever steps are required,” said the state minister.
The government will certainly take all legal measures needed to bring the accused back to face justice, she added.
Asked whether Bangladesh has received any response from India to its earlier letter seeking the extradition of former home minister Asaduzzaman Khan Kamal, Shama said diplomatic communication is ongoing. “We have not yet received a definitive answer from India,” she said.
“However, from what we understand, they may have their own internal legal procedures to follow, and they are carrying out that process. These efforts will continue until we successfully bring them back to Bangladeshi soil,” she added.
Indian media outlet The Print claimed that India has not yet given its approval to Bangladesh for the appointment of Asad Alam Siam as Dhaka’s next high commissioner at New Delhi though the process to appoint new high commissioners and ambassadors by Dhaka for various foreign postings began in July.
Asked about media reports in Bangladesh and India, Shama urged the media not to publish such reports without official confirmation.
“I would request everyone not to pay heed to or publish such news reports until an official statement or concrete information is issued by either the Bangladesh Ministry of Foreign Affairs or the Government of India,” she said.
On an inter-ministerial meeting held on Tuesday regarding Bangladeshis travelling abroad with forged documents and false information, the state minister said the government is working to streamline the migration process for the large number of Bangladeshis living abroad.
“Ever since the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) formed the government, we have been working on how to streamline and consolidate the migration process for the vast number of Bangladeshi citizens living abroad,” she said.
The state minister noted that the Ministry of Foreign Affairs had already taken several initiatives, including opening a dedicated Migration Wing.

item.title: RAB begins operations as Special Response Battalion
item.description:
The Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) has been dissolved and begun operating as the Special Response Battalion (SRB) under the police, with the new unit starting operations on Wednesday.
RAB chief Ahsan Habib Palash confirmed the development. He said: “A gazette has been published under the name ‘Special Response Battalion (SRB).’”
All RAB activities have been carried out under the name SRB since Wednesday following the change. The new name was also reflected in an invitation letter issued for a press conference.
Meanwhile, the government published the gazette notification of the Special Response Battalion Act, 2026, on Tuesday.
The notification states that once the law takes effect, only those provisions of the Armed Police Battalions Ordinance, 1979, that were incorporated to provide the legal basis for forming RAB will be repealed.
However, the RAB (Court Procedures and Departmental Proceedings) Rules, 2005, issued under Section 14 of the ordinance, will remain in force.
Any departmental disciplinary action or court proceedings against a member of the unit under these rules or any other law or regulation will also remain valid and enforceable.
The SRB law further states that relevant RAB personnel, along with its orders, powers, authority, existing facilities, funds, cash and money in bank accounts, liabilities, contracts, movable and immovable property, account books, registers, records and related documents, will be transferred to and vested in the SRB immediately.
Amid objections from the opposition, Parliament passed a bill on Thursday to establish the SRB as a specialized unit. The government has now published the gazette notification of the law.
In 2003, amendments to the Armed Police Battalions Ordinance provided the legal basis for forming RAB. The force subsequently faced criticism over various activities.
The United Nations, the Commission of Inquiry on Enforced Disappearances, and domestic and international human rights organizations have at various times recommended the dissolution of RAB in light of its past activities.
On December 10, 2021, the United States imposed sanctions on RAB and 7 serving and former senior officials of the force over allegations of human rights violations.

item.title: Teacher killed in snatching: Motorcycle used in incident recovered, 2 arrested

The Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DB) has arrested two more people in connection with the death of headmistress Ronjina Parveen, 55, who fell from a rickshaw after being pulled by snatchers in front of the South Plaza of the National Parliament House.
Police also recovered the motorcycle allegedly used in the snatching and Ronjina’s handbag.
Md Shafiqul Islam, additional police commissioner of the DB, confirmed the arrests and recoveries on Wednesday.
He said Ronjina’s handbag, along with a bus ticket found inside it, had been recovered. He said further details would be disclosed at a press conference at the DMP Media Centre on Wednesday afternoon.
Earlier, on August 30, the Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) arrested Md Mosharraf Hossain Poni alias Poni Gazi and his associate Cedric in connection with the case.
At the time, RAB said it had recovered a Yamaha R15 motorcycle from them and claimed that it was the motorcycle used in the snatching.
Following the RAB briefing, however, Mosharraf told journalists that he was not involved in the incident. He also claimed that his motorcycle did not resemble the one used in the snatching.
CCTV footage recorded during the incident showed a blue motorcycle, while the motorcycle recovered by RAB was black and white, raising questions over whether it was the same vehicle.
The latest recovery is expected to clarify the discrepancy.

item.title: Moody's updates Bangladesh’s outlook to ‘stable’
item.description:
Moody’s Ratings has updated Bangladesh’s sovereign outlook from ‘negative’ to ‘stable,’ citing reduced political tension, higher foreign exchange reserves, and historic remittance levels.
In its latest evaluation, Moody’s noted that post-election stability and strong public support for the new government have minimized risks to ongoing reforms. Financial backing from the IMF and other international institutions remains vital.
Moody's had previously lowered Bangladesh’s rating from 'B1' to 'B2' in March 2025 with a negative outlook, pointing to bank asset degradation, high inflation, and sluggish growth.
The long-term issuer and senior unsecured ratings stay at ‘B2,’ while the short-term rating remains ‘Not Prime.’
Banking insiders expect this adjustment to expand foreign credit lines for local banks, aiding trade imports.
Moody’s reported reserves grew to roughly $32.9 billion by mid-2026—covering over four months of imports—up from $21.4 billion in 2024. This recovery was fueled by formal remittance channels, flexible exchange policies, and market-driven currency reforms.
Economic expansion is projected to recover slowly, moving from 3.5% in FY2024–25 to 4.1% in FY2025–26, 4.3% in FY2026–27, and potentially 4.9% in FY2027–28 as industrial output stabilizes.
Inflation is expected to hover around 9%.
The sovereign rating was capped at ‘B2’ due to systemic financial sector vulnerabilities, with non-performing loans (NPLs) hitting approximately 32.8% of total loans.
Addressing these capital deficits to meet international standards could require recapitalization equal to 10% of GDP, placing severe strain on public finances.
However, a 12% annual surge in deposits through March 2026 suggests the sector suffers from structural bad debt rather than liquidity shortages.
Bangladesh's low tax-to-GDP ratio restricts fiscal policy, with debt interest payments consuming nearly 30% of government revenue, even though overall public debt stays manageable.
Additional hazards include energy infrastructure vulnerabilities highlighted by recent LNG terminal disruptions, alongside potential losses in trade preferences and concessional loans as Bangladesh graduates from LDC status.

item.title: Humaiun Kobir stresses stronger global cooperation on health, SDGs
item.description:
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir on Wednesday underscored the importance of international cooperation and multilateral partnerships in advancing health and achieving sustainable development goals.
He held a meeting with Dr Ahmed Jamsheed Mohamed, representative of the World Health Organization (WHO), at his office and discussed issues of mutual interest.
During the meeting, the state minister and the WHO Representative discussed matters of mutual interest, with particular emphasis on strengthening cooperation in the areas of public health, health security, disease prevention, and access to essential health services.
He appreciated the WHO’s continued cooperation and support in strengthening the country’s health sector and addressing emerging public health challenges.
The WHO Representative briefed the State Minister on the organization’s ongoing and planned cooperation in Bangladesh including support for health-system strengthening, capacity building, disease surveillance, and preparedness for public health emergencies.
Both sides expressed their commitment to further strengthening collaboration between Bangladesh and the WHO and agreed to continue close coordination on issues of common interest at national, regional, and international levels.

item.title: Complaint filed against 5 over alleged enforced disappearance, murder
item.description:
A formal complaint has been filed with the International Crimes Tribunal against five people, including former CTTC chief Asaduzzaman Miah and Additional Deputy Commissioner Ishtiaq Ahmed.
The complaint concerns the alleged enforced disappearance and murder of Abul Hossain Al Amin, principal of Ibn Masud Madrasa in Chattar, Gazipur.
Rashed Khan, political assistant to Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, filed the complaint with the tribunal on Wednesday.
Earlier, the tribunal's investigation agency submitted its report to the prosecution, implicating five people, including then CTTC chief Asaduzzaman, ADC Ishtiaq Ahmed and then police inspector Asaduzzaman Miah.
According to sources familiar with the investigation, a group posing as Detective Branch (DB) police abducted Al Amin from Ibn Masud Madrasa in Gazipur on January 30, 2023. He has not been seen or heard from since.
The investigation report said Al Amin was tortured after being detained and allegedly died from the torture. His body was subsequently dumped in the Dhaleshwari River, according to the report.
The report said the CTTC unit arrested six people from different parts of the country on January 28, 2023. Based on information obtained during remand interrogations, a team led by then CTTC ADC Ishtiaq Ahmed detained Al Amin from the madrasa on January 30.
It was alleged that Al Amin was subjected to physical torture for 18 consecutive days at the CTTC office on Minto Road. He became critically ill and later died at the Central Police Hospital, according to the investigation report.
The report further alleged that the accused sought to conceal his death by dumping his body into the Dhaleshwari River from Tulsikhali Bridge in Keraniganj.

item.title: Teesta erosion leaves several hundred families homeless in northern districts
item.description:
At least 386 houses have been washed away by severe erosion along the Teesta River in five northern districts over the past seven days, leaving hundreds of families homeless.
The erosion has intensified at 113 points in Rangpur, Gaibandha, Lalmonirhat, Nilphamari and Kurigram, according to the Bangladesh Water Development Board (BWDB).
Ahsan Habib, superintending engineer of the BWDB Rangpur regional office, said the situation has worsened rapidly in recent days.
“Erosion has intensified at 113 points in the five districts while 386 houses have been washed away in the past seven days,” he said.
He said there was insufficient allocation for erosion-control measures and the matter has been brought to the ministry’s attention.
In Gaibandha’s Sundarganj upazila, erosion has taken a particularly heavy toll on people living along the riverbank in Kapasia Union.
In Singijani and Bhorer Pakhi areas, residents said the river current increased suddenly, causing sections of the riverbank to collapse one after another.
Many families could not save their furniture, rice, clothes and other belongings as their houses collapsed.
Shahidul Islam, a resident of the area, said the erosion was so rapid that people barely had time to move their belongings to safety.
Ahad Mia said families are now facing an uncertain future after losing their homes and land.
Sundarganj Upazila Nirbahi Officer Iffat Jahan Tuli visited the affected areas and assured them of necessary assistance.
Gaibandha BWDB Executive Engineer Shariful Islam said geo-bags are being dumped at vulnerable points as an immediate measure.
“We are monitoring the situation and taking immediate preventive measures. Further steps will be taken based on the situation,” he said.
The erosion has also intensified in Kurigram’s Ulipur and Rajarhat upazilas, where around 80 houses have been washed away in the past week.
Families who have lost their homes are struggling to find safe places for themselves, their children and livestock.
In Lalmonirhat, all five upazilas have been affected by erosion.
BWDB Executive Engineer Sunil Roy said the intensity of erosion is increasing with fluctuations in the river’s water level.
Geo-textile materials have been placed at some vulnerable locations, he said but there was no allocation for permanent erosion-control work.
“As there is no allocation for permanent erosion-control work, there is little we can do beyond taking immediate measures,” he said.
Khuliagachh Union Parishad Chairman Khairuzzaman Badal said erosion is continuing almost every day.
In Rangpur, 53 houses have been washed away in Pirgachha, Kaunia and Gangachara upazilas during the past seven days, said BWDB Executive Engineer Hafiz Uddin.
The affected people said they needed permanent protection rather than temporary relief.
In Nilphamari, hundreds of erosion-hit families are spending their days in open spaces, on embankments or in relatives’ yards.
Many families have no arrangements for cooking and food, while residents said tents and dry food were urgently needed.
Abdul Karim of Char Kharibari said the river has eroded the area six times in two years.
“I have lost two houses to the river. Now I don’t know where to go,” he said.
Atwar Rahman said authorities often took measures only after houses began to collapse, rather than taking permanent steps to protect riverbank communities.
